title.raw: VoIP Phone Systems for Law Firms: RingCentral vs Nextiva vs Ooma (2026)
title.rendered: VoIP Phone Systems for Law Firms: RingCentral vs Nextiva vs Ooma (2026)

content.raw:
This article is general information, not legal advice. Check recording, texting and ethics questions with your state bar or counsel.

Quick answer: a hosted VoIP phone system for law firms moves your phone lines onto the internet, so calls ring on desk phones, computers and mobile apps. RingCentral, Nextiva and Ooma all sell this, and the right pick depends mostly on whether you need built-in texting, call recording and a Clio connection at your price point. Ooma is the simplest, lowest-priced entry; RingCentral has the broadest plan ladder; Nextiva has the lowest annual entry price but the steepest jump when billed monthly.

Key takeaways

  • Prices below are per user per month from each vendor's own page as of November 2026, before taxes and fees. They change, so confirm before you buy.
  • Annual billing is much cheaper than monthly at RingCentral and Nextiva. Ooma lists its plans as "No Contract Necessary."
  • Recording, texting and CRM features are tied to plan level. Check the plan, not just the brand.
  • Recording consent rules differ by state. Learn your state's rule and plan a greeting before you turn recording on.
  • Texting clients from a business number needs carrier registration (10DLC). Ask each vendor how it is handled and what it costs.

How we compared these VoIP phone systems

This comparison is based on each vendor's official pricing and product pages, opened in November 2026. We have not run hands-on call-quality tests, and we do not give ratings or scores. Where a page did not state something, we say so and tell you to ask the vendor. Some pages show different content by region, plan size or sign-in state, so treat every number as "check the pricing page" rather than a quote.

Which VoIP phone system is best for a small law firm?

There is no single winner. Match the system to how your firm actually uses the phone:

  • Solo or two-lawyer firm that wants simple and cheap: Ooma Office Essentials or Pro, because the list prices are flat per user and no contract is required.
  • Firm that wants the biggest plan ladder, a Clio-related app option and add-ons: RingCentral (RingEX), with the caveat that Clio logging appears through a third-party app on RingCentral's own app gallery.
  • Firm that will commit to a year and wants the lowest annual per-user price: Nextiva NEXT Core, but read what is and is not in that plan.
  • Firm that needs texting clients regularly: compare the monthly text allowances in the table, then ask about registration.

RingCentral vs Nextiva vs Ooma: how much do they cost per user?

Here are the entry and mid-tier plans as published in November 2026. Prices exclude taxes and fees, and RingCentral's figures are those shown for the 1 to 5 user selection on its page.

Sources: RingCentral plans and pricing, Nextiva pricing and Ooma Office plans.

Annual vs monthly billing and minimum users

  • RingCentral: the page says you can save up to 33% by paying annually and lets you pick a user count (1-5, 6-100, 100+). Always select your real headcount, since the page is built around those tiers.
  • Nextiva: the page toggles Monthly and Annually and says annual Small Business pricing applies to new customers with 1 to 100 employees on a paid term of 12 months or longer. Add-ons are billed separately.
  • Ooma: each plan is labeled "No Contract Necessary" and the page says applicable taxes and fees are not included. It does not state a separate annual discount on the page we opened, so ask sales.

Do not forget the extras. RingCentral's page notes that taxes and fees (including an E911 service fee) may apply, and that phone rental needs a multi-year contract. Desk phones are bought separately at Nextiva. Ask each vendor for an all-in monthly total for your headcount.

Can a VoIP phone system record calls, and is it legal?

Yes, all three list call recording, but where it sits depends on the plan. RingCentral lists on-demand recording on Core. Nextiva's comparison table shows call recording on its NEXT plans. Ooma lists call recording on Pro (its page describes on-demand and always-on recording under its feature list). Confirm retention length and who can access the files.

Whether recording is lawful depends on where the parties are. Some states let one participant consent to a recording (often called one-party consent). Others require everyone on the call to consent (all-party). A call between your office and a client in another state can raise both rules. The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press keeps a state-by-state recording guide that explains this at a general level, and it says to talk with a lawyer for your situation.

Practical habits that fit most firms, again as general information: tell callers at the start, put the notice in your auto-attendant greeting, record only when you have a reason, and treat recordings as confidential client material with limited access. Ask your state bar whether any ethics opinion covers recording clients.

How do auto-attendant, call routing and after-hours calls work?

An auto-attendant (or virtual receptionist) is the automated greeting that says "Press 1 for..." and sends callers to the right person. All three vendors describe one: Ooma lists a virtual receptionist even on Essentials, RingCentral includes auto attendant in its feature set, and Nextiva lists Smart Call Routing (Simple IVR) on every NEXT plan.

A sensible small-firm setup is below.

  1. Set business hours in the system so the greeting changes by time of day.
  2. Daytime: a short menu (existing client, new matter, billing), then a ring group, then voicemail sent to email.
  3. After hours: forward to a live answering service or an AI receptionist, with a single urgent route to the on-call lawyer.
  4. Test every path from an outside mobile phone before you publish the number.

If you want people to answer overflow and after-hours calls, see our comparison of Smith.ai vs Ruby virtual receptionists. Several VoIP vendors also sell their own AI receptionist add-ons (RingCentral lists one starting at $39, per its page); check how it handles intake and what it should never be allowed to say.

Callers often book consultations from the same call flow, so pair routing with an appointment scheduling tool.

Can a law firm text clients from a VoIP number?

Yes, but not for free-for-all volume. Business texting from a regular local number is regulated by carriers under "10DLC" (10-digit long code) rules: the business registers its brand and use case through a registry so carriers know the texts are legitimate. RingCentral's page states that The Campaign Registry (TCR) registration is required for SMS/MMS and that additional TCR fees may apply. We could not verify Nextiva's or Ooma's registration fees from the pages we opened, so ask both.

Allowances differ widely, as the table shows: RingCentral Core includes 25 SMS per user per month, Nextiva NEXT Core 100 texts per user, and Ooma Pro up to 250 per month. Marketing or high-volume texting is a separate product at RingCentral (High Volume SMS, priced per message). For a law firm, keep texts to scheduling and logistics and avoid putting case details in them; check your state bar guidance on client communications. Texting rules for marketing (consent, opt-out) are their own area, so ask counsel.

Does it work with Clio and other legal software?

Only count an integration if the vendor lists it. What we found on official pages in November 2026:

  • Ooma: its Office plans page lists Clio in its integrations, describing it as helping law offices capture every billable moment. It does not say in the text we read which plan includes it, so ask sales (Pro Plus lists "CRM Integration").
  • RingCentral: the RingCentral app gallery page mentions Clio through a third-party service, CallConnector.ai, which says it logs calls into Clio Manage and Clio Grow and has its own pricing. That is separate from RingCentral's plans. RingEX Advanced lists "CRM integrations" generally.
  • Nextiva: we did not find Clio on its integrations page. Its pricing page lists Outlook and Google contact sync, Salesforce and single sign-on. Ask whether a Clio connection exists or can be built through its API.

Before you commit, ask for the exact steps: does a call create a time entry, attach to a matter, or only show a call pop? That distinction is what saves billable minutes.

How do you keep your existing phone number?

Moving your current number to a new carrier is called porting. Ooma lists "Free Number Transfer" on its plans page. RingCentral and Nextiva both support bringing numbers, but we did not see porting terms or fees on the pages we opened, so ask. Practical steps:

  1. Get a recent bill from your current carrier and your account number or PIN.
  2. List every number to move: main line, fax, direct dials, and any that forward elsewhere.
  3. Ask the new vendor for a target date, and do not cancel the old service until the port completes.
  4. Have a temporary forwarding number ready in case the cutover is late.

Softphone apps, desk phones and mobile use

A softphone is the phone in an app. RingCentral says its app works on Windows, macOS, Android and iOS. Ooma lists a mobile app on every plan and a desktop app starting with Pro. Nextiva lists mobile on its NEXT plans and says VoIP desk phones work with every plan, bought separately. Lawyers working from home or court can then use the firm number without giving out a cell number. Check call forwarding and caller-ID settings so your outbound calls show the office number.

Your phones depend on your internet. A stable connection and a good router matter more than the vendor logo, and your website and email domain should stay under your own control. For email and calendar alongside the phone, see Microsoft 365 setup for law firms or Google Workspace setup for law firms, and keep the main number on your site consistent with your Google Business Profile.

What about 911 and emergency calls on VoIP?

VoIP 911 needs a registered address, because the call travels over the internet rather than a fixed line. Update the address whenever a user moves or works from a new place. RingCentral's E911 cost recovery page notes a 911 service fee, which is not a government-mandated charge. Ooma lists a 911 service on its plans page. Ask each vendor how to set addresses per user, and what happens during an internet or power outage.

Which one should you pick? A short decision guide

Next, try the one you shortlist on a trial or demo with your real headcount, test the call flow from outside phones, and get the all-in price in writing. RingCentral's page describes a 14-day free trial for new subscribers (SMS is not available in the trial).

Alternatives to consider

  • Your existing carrier or cable provider: may bundle a hosted phone system with internet; compare features and contract length.
  • A virtual receptionist service only: if you mainly want someone answering, see Smith.ai vs Ruby and keep a simple mobile or softphone line.
  • Microsoft Teams Phone or a Google Voice plan: worth a look if you already live in those suites. We did not review their pricing here.

FAQ

How much does a VoIP phone system for a law firm cost?

From the vendors' November 2026 pages, entry plans run roughly $15 to $30 per user per month depending on vendor and billing term, before taxes, fees and hardware. See the table above and each pricing page.

Is call recording on a VoIP system legal?

It depends on state law. Some states need one party's consent; others need everyone's. This is general information, not legal advice. Check your state and your bar's guidance.

Can I keep my current office number?

Usually yes through porting. Ooma lists free number transfer. Ask the other vendors about terms and timing, and do not cancel your old service early.

Do I need 10DLC registration to text clients?

If you text from a standard local business number, carriers expect registration. RingCentral says TCR registration is required for SMS/MMS and fees may apply. Ask your vendor how it is handled.

Does RingCentral, Nextiva or Ooma integrate with Clio?

Ooma lists Clio on its plans page. RingCentral's app gallery points to a third-party Clio logging app. We did not find Clio on Nextiva's integrations page. Verify before buying.

This article is general information, not legal advice. Check recording, texting and ethics questions with your state bar or counsel.

Quick answer: a hosted VoIP phone system for law firms moves your phone lines onto the internet, so calls ring on desk phones, computers and mobile apps. RingCentral, Nextiva and Ooma all sell this, and the right pick depends mostly on whether you need built-in texting, call recording and a Clio connection at your price point. Ooma is the simplest, lowest-priced entry; RingCentral has the broadest plan ladder; Nextiva has the lowest annual entry price but the steepest jump when billed monthly.

Key takeaways

  • Prices below are per user per month from each vendor’s own page as of November 2026, before taxes and fees. They change, so confirm before you buy.
  • Annual billing is much cheaper than monthly at RingCentral and Nextiva. Ooma lists its plans as “No Contract Necessary.”
  • Recording, texting and CRM features are tied to plan level. Check the plan, not just the brand.
  • Recording consent rules differ by state. Learn your state’s rule and plan a greeting before you turn recording on.
  • Texting clients from a business number needs carrier registration (10DLC). Ask each vendor how it is handled and what it costs.

How we compared these VoIP phone systems

This comparison is based on each vendor’s official pricing and product pages, opened in November 2026. We have not run hands-on call-quality tests, and we do not give ratings or scores. Where a page did not state something, we say so and tell you to ask the vendor. Some pages show different content by region, plan size or sign-in state, so treat every number as “check the pricing page” rather than a quote.

Which VoIP phone system is best for a small law firm?

There is no single winner. Match the system to how your firm actually uses the phone:

  • Solo or two-lawyer firm that wants simple and cheap: Ooma Office Essentials or Pro, because the list prices are flat per user and no contract is required.
  • Firm that wants the biggest plan ladder, a Clio-related app option and add-ons: RingCentral (RingEX), with the caveat that Clio logging appears through a third-party app on RingCentral’s own app gallery.
  • Firm that will commit to a year and wants the lowest annual per-user price: Nextiva NEXT Core, but read what is and is not in that plan.
  • Firm that needs texting clients regularly: compare the monthly text allowances in the table, then ask about registration.

RingCentral vs Nextiva vs Ooma: how much do they cost per user?

Here are the entry and mid-tier plans as published in November 2026. Prices exclude taxes and fees, and RingCentral’s figures are those shown for the 1 to 5 user selection on its page.

Sources: RingCentral plans and pricing, Nextiva pricing and Ooma Office plans.

Annual vs monthly billing and minimum users

  • RingCentral: the page says you can save up to 33% by paying annually and lets you pick a user count (1-5, 6-100, 100+). Always select your real headcount, since the page is built around those tiers.
  • Nextiva: the page toggles Monthly and Annually and says annual Small Business pricing applies to new customers with 1 to 100 employees on a paid term of 12 months or longer. Add-ons are billed separately.
  • Ooma: each plan is labeled “No Contract Necessary” and the page says applicable taxes and fees are not included. It does not state a separate annual discount on the page we opened, so ask sales.

Do not forget the extras. RingCentral’s page notes that taxes and fees (including an E911 service fee) may apply, and that phone rental needs a multi-year contract. Desk phones are bought separately at Nextiva. Ask each vendor for an all-in monthly total for your headcount.

Can a VoIP phone system record calls, and is it legal?

Yes, all three list call recording, but where it sits depends on the plan. RingCentral lists on-demand recording on Core. Nextiva’s comparison table shows call recording on its NEXT plans. Ooma lists call recording on Pro (its page describes on-demand and always-on recording under its feature list). Confirm retention length and who can access the files.

Whether recording is lawful depends on where the parties are. Some states let one participant consent to a recording (often called one-party consent). Others require everyone on the call to consent (all-party). A call between your office and a client in another state can raise both rules. The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press keeps a state-by-state recording guide that explains this at a general level, and it says to talk with a lawyer for your situation.

Practical habits that fit most firms, again as general information: tell callers at the start, put the notice in your auto-attendant greeting, record only when you have a reason, and treat recordings as confidential client material with limited access. Ask your state bar whether any ethics opinion covers recording clients.

How do auto-attendant, call routing and after-hours calls work?

An auto-attendant (or virtual receptionist) is the automated greeting that says “Press 1 for…” and sends callers to the right person. All three vendors describe one: Ooma lists a virtual receptionist even on Essentials, RingCentral includes auto attendant in its feature set, and Nextiva lists Smart Call Routing (Simple IVR) on every NEXT plan.

A sensible small-firm setup is below.

  1. Set business hours in the system so the greeting changes by time of day.
  2. Daytime: a short menu (existing client, new matter, billing), then a ring group, then voicemail sent to email.
  3. After hours: forward to a live answering service or an AI receptionist, with a single urgent route to the on-call lawyer.
  4. Test every path from an outside mobile phone before you publish the number.

If you want people to answer overflow and after-hours calls, see our comparison of Smith.ai vs Ruby virtual receptionists. Several VoIP vendors also sell their own AI receptionist add-ons (RingCentral lists one starting at $39, per its page); check how it handles intake and what it should never be allowed to say.

Callers often book consultations from the same call flow, so pair routing with an appointment scheduling tool.

Can a law firm text clients from a VoIP number?

Yes, but not for free-for-all volume. Business texting from a regular local number is regulated by carriers under “10DLC” (10-digit long code) rules: the business registers its brand and use case through a registry so carriers know the texts are legitimate. RingCentral’s page states that The Campaign Registry (TCR) registration is required for SMS/MMS and that additional TCR fees may apply. We could not verify Nextiva’s or Ooma’s registration fees from the pages we opened, so ask both.

Allowances differ widely, as the table shows: RingCentral Core includes 25 SMS per user per month, Nextiva NEXT Core 100 texts per user, and Ooma Pro up to 250 per month. Marketing or high-volume texting is a separate product at RingCentral (High Volume SMS, priced per message). For a law firm, keep texts to scheduling and logistics and avoid putting case details in them; check your state bar guidance on client communications. Texting rules for marketing (consent, opt-out) are their own area, so ask counsel.

Does it work with Clio and other legal software?

Only count an integration if the vendor lists it. What we found on official pages in November 2026:

  • Ooma: its Office plans page lists Clio in its integrations, describing it as helping law offices capture every billable moment. It does not say in the text we read which plan includes it, so ask sales (Pro Plus lists “CRM Integration”).
  • RingCentral: the RingCentral app gallery page mentions Clio through a third-party service, CallConnector.ai, which says it logs calls into Clio Manage and Clio Grow and has its own pricing. That is separate from RingCentral’s plans. RingEX Advanced lists “CRM integrations” generally.
  • Nextiva: we did not find Clio on its integrations page. Its pricing page lists Outlook and Google contact sync, Salesforce and single sign-on. Ask whether a Clio connection exists or can be built through its API.

Before you commit, ask for the exact steps: does a call create a time entry, attach to a matter, or only show a call pop? That distinction is what saves billable minutes.

How do you keep your existing phone number?

Moving your current number to a new carrier is called porting. Ooma lists “Free Number Transfer” on its plans page. RingCentral and Nextiva both support bringing numbers, but we did not see porting terms or fees on the pages we opened, so ask. Practical steps:

  1. Get a recent bill from your current carrier and your account number or PIN.
  2. List every number to move: main line, fax, direct dials, and any that forward elsewhere.
  3. Ask the new vendor for a target date, and do not cancel the old service until the port completes.
  4. Have a temporary forwarding number ready in case the cutover is late.

Softphone apps, desk phones and mobile use

A softphone is the phone in an app. RingCentral says its app works on Windows, macOS, Android and iOS. Ooma lists a mobile app on every plan and a desktop app starting with Pro. Nextiva lists mobile on its NEXT plans and says VoIP desk phones work with every plan, bought separately. Lawyers working from home or court can then use the firm number without giving out a cell number. Check call forwarding and caller-ID settings so your outbound calls show the office number.

Your phones depend on your internet. A stable connection and a good router matter more than the vendor logo, and your website and email domain should stay under your own control. For email and calendar alongside the phone, see Microsoft 365 setup for law firms or Google Workspace setup for law firms, and keep the main number on your site consistent with your Google Business Profile.

What about 911 and emergency calls on VoIP?

VoIP 911 needs a registered address, because the call travels over the internet rather than a fixed line. Update the address whenever a user moves or works from a new place. RingCentral’s E911 cost recovery page notes a 911 service fee, which is not a government-mandated charge. Ooma lists a 911 service on its plans page. Ask each vendor how to set addresses per user, and what happens during an internet or power outage.

Which one should you pick? A short decision guide

Next, try the one you shortlist on a trial or demo with your real headcount, test the call flow from outside phones, and get the all-in price in writing. RingCentral’s page describes a 14-day free trial for new subscribers (SMS is not available in the trial).

Alternatives to consider

  • Your existing carrier or cable provider: may bundle a hosted phone system with internet; compare features and contract length.
  • A virtual receptionist service only: if you mainly want someone answering, see Smith.ai vs Ruby and keep a simple mobile or softphone line.
  • Microsoft Teams Phone or a Google Voice plan: worth a look if you already live in those suites. We did not review their pricing here.

How much does a VoIP phone system for a law firm cost?

From the vendors’ November 2026 pages, entry plans run roughly $15 to $30 per user per month depending on vendor and billing term, before taxes, fees and hardware. See the table above and each pricing page.

It depends on state law. Some states need one party’s consent; others need everyone’s. This is general information, not legal advice. Check your state and your bar’s guidance.

Can I keep my current office number?

Usually yes through porting. Ooma lists free number transfer. Ask the other vendors about terms and timing, and do not cancel your old service early.

If you text from a standard local business number, carriers expect registration. RingCentral says TCR registration is required for SMS/MMS and fees may apply. Ask your vendor how it is handled.

Does RingCentral, Nextiva or Ooma integrate with Clio?

Ooma lists Clio on its plans page. RingCentral’s app gallery points to a third-party Clio logging app. We did not find Clio on Nextiva’s integrations page. Verify before buying.

title.raw: Law Firm Website Hacked? A Step-by-Step Recovery Plan (2026)
title.rendered: Law Firm Website Hacked? A Step-by-Step Recovery Plan (2026)

content.raw:
Quick answer: If your law firm website is hacked, do not panic and do not start deleting things. Call your host, put the site into maintenance mode, save a copy of the files and logs, change every password, scan, then either restore a clean backup or clean the site. Ask Google to review it only after everything is fixed. Because a firm website can touch client information, also think through your ethics duties early.

Key takeaways

  • Preserve evidence before you clean. A copy of the infected site and your logs helps you (or an expert) find how the attacker got in.
  • Changing the WordPress password is not enough. Change hosting, SFTP, database, domain and email passwords too, then again after cleanup.
  • Restoring a backup only works if the backup predates the hack and you close the hole it came through.
  • Google only reviews a site after you fix every issue on every page. One request, not repeated ones.
  • If client confidential information may have been exposed, ABA Formal Opinion 483 says to act promptly, investigate and consider notice. State laws add their own rules.

How do I know my law firm website was hacked?

A hacked website is one where someone gained unauthorized access and changed files, content or settings. The WordPress.org documentation lists the clear signs it calls indicators of compromise (WordPress.org: My site was hacked):

  • Your site is blacklisted by Google, Bing or similar services, or flagged for distributing malware.
  • Your host has disabled the site.
  • Visitors say their antivirus is flagging it.
  • Someone tells you your site is being used to attack other sites.
  • Unauthorized changes appear, such as new user accounts.
  • You can see the defacement, or odd pages and redirects, when you open the site.

Other practical clues: search results showing pharmaceutical or gambling titles under your domain, contact-form emails that stopped arriving, or admin users you do not recognize. A site that is merely slow or down may not be hacked at all, so ask your host to confirm.

What should I do in the first hour?

  1. Stay calm and write things down. Note what you saw, when (with time zone), and what changed recently, such as a new plugin or theme update. WordPress.org calls this the start of an incident report.
  2. Call your host. On shared hosting the problem may reach beyond your site, and the host can confirm whether it is a hack or a service problem. Ask what backups exist and how far back they go.
  3. Take the site offline or into maintenance mode. This protects visitors and stops further damage. Your host can often do this at the server level if you cannot log in.
  4. Preserve evidence. Before cleaning, take a snapshot of the files and database as they are, and ask the host to keep access and error logs. WordPress.org recommends taking one more snapshot before cleanup, even if it is infected.
  5. Scan your own computer. WordPress.org notes infections often start on a local machine that captures logins. Run a full antivirus scan on every device used to manage the site.
  6. Check email. If the site was sending spam, your server may be blacklisted. If your email runs on the same server, see our guide to law firm domain email, SPF, DKIM and DMARC.

How do I change passwords and lock the attacker out?

Reset every access point, not only the WordPress login. Use long, unique passwords from a manager (see our password manager guide for law firms) and turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) wherever it is offered.

  • Force a password reset for all WordPress users, especially administrators, and delete accounts you do not recognize.
  • Replace the security keys and salts in wp-config.php. WordPress.org says this logs out anyone still signed in, including an attacker. It offers a generator at api.wordpress.org/secret-key/1.1/salt/.
  • Do not forget SFTP, hosting control panel and database credentials.

Do it twice. WordPress.org advises changing passwords again once you are certain the site is clean, because an attacker may have captured the first new ones.

How do I scan a hacked WordPress site?

Use two kinds of scanner together. WordPress.org says no single solution is best, but combining them improves your odds. A remote scanner looks at your site from the outside. An application scanner (a plugin) looks at files from the inside.

A clean SiteCheck result is not proof of a clean site, because of the limits Sucuri itself lists. For a comparison of the plugins, see WordPress security plugins for law firms.

Should I clean the site or restore a backup?

Restore if you have a backup from before the first sign of trouble. Clean in place if you do not. Either way, you must find and close the way in, or the attacker returns.

Restoring a clean backup

Work out when the infection began (file dates, logs, first symptom), then pick a backup older than that. After restoring, update every plugin, theme and WordPress itself right away, since an outdated component is a common way in. Any content you added after the backup date must be re-entered.

Cleaning in place

The WordPress.org guidance suggests these steps:

  • Replace /wp-admin and /wp-includes with fresh copies of the same version of WordPress, uploaded by SFTP. It warns that the dashboard reinstall option often only overwrites existing files, while hacks add new ones.
  • Inspect wp-content: delete plugins and themes you do not use and reinstall the rest from official sources.
  • Check .htaccess, the file most often altered, plus index.php, header.php, footer.php and functions.php in your theme.
  • Look for backdoors: hidden files that let the attacker back in even after you change passwords. Also remove unknown admin users, and check scheduled tasks and the database for injected content.

Backdoors are hard to find by eye. If you are not comfortable in files and databases, this is the point to bring in help.

When should I call a professional cleanup service?

  • The site is reinfected after cleaning.
  • Your host has suspended the account or will not restore it.
  • Client information may have been exposed (a developer or security firm can help determine what happened).
  • You cannot log in, or cannot tell which backup is clean.
  • You do not have the time. Downtime costs a firm leads.

Options: your host (some include cleanup), a malware-removal service such as Sucuri (see our tool comparisons hub), or a WordPress developer. Ask what is included, how long it takes, and whether they will explain how the attacker got in.

How do I get Google to remove the hacked warning?

Fix everything first, then request a review in Search Console. Google’s Security Issues report covers three categories: hacked content, malware and unwanted software, and social engineering. If you have not set up Search Console, our GA4 and Search Console setup guide walks through it. You will need verified ownership to see the report.

  1. Open the Security Issues report and expand each issue. Use the sample URLs to find the problem; the list is a sample, not necessarily complete.
  2. Fix the issue across the whole site and fix every issue listed. Google says fixing only some pages will not earn a partial return to search results.
  3. Test your fixes, and make sure the pages are not blocked from Google by login, robots.txt or noindex.
  4. Select Request Review. Explain the issue, the steps you took and the outcome.
  5. Wait. Google says most reviews take several days or weeks, with emails when the request is received and completed. Do not resubmit while pending.

Sources: Security Issues report and Manual Actions report help pages. Other blocklists (Bing, antivirus vendors) have their own removal processes; WordPress.org recommends registering with the major webmaster consoles.

Could my contact form or intake data have been exposed?

Possibly, and for a law firm this is the question that matters most. Check where form submissions go. Some plugins store entries in the WordPress database, which an attacker with admin or database access could read. Others only email you. Review: stored form entries, uploaded files in the media library, user accounts, and any email or CRM integrations whose keys sit in the site settings. If entries were stored, assume they could have been read and note what they contained. Afterward, follow our guide to a secure contact form for a law firm website and avoid storing sensitive details on the site at all.

What are a lawyer’s ethics duties after a website hack?

This is general information, not legal advice. Check with your state bar or ethics counsel. ABA Formal Opinion 483 (October 2018), “Lawyers’ Obligations After an Electronic Data Breach or Cyberattack,” addresses what lawyers should do when client confidential information may be compromised. As summarized by secondary sources (the ABA site blocked our automated access, so we could not read the opinion itself), it points to these duties:

  • Monitor so a breach is detected, which is part of a firm having reasonable security.
  • Act promptly to stop the breach and limit the damage, then restore systems.
  • Make reasonable efforts to determine what occurred: what was accessed and whose information it was.
  • Consider notifying clients when material client confidential information was compromised, tied to the duty to keep clients informed.

The opinion deals with ethics rules only. State data-breach notification laws vary, as do their triggers and deadlines, and your cyber insurance policy may require quick notice to the insurer. A marketing site with no client data is a different situation from one holding stored intake forms. Keep your incident notes: what you found, when, and what you did. They support any decision on notice.

How do I prevent it from happening again?

  • Put a web application firewall (WAF) in front of the site. See Cloudflare for law firm websites or a security plugin comparison.
  • Keep WordPress, themes and plugins updated and remove unused ones.
  • Use 2FA and unique passwords; give each person their own login.
  • Run automatic offsite backups and test a restore.
  • Work through the law firm website security checklist and consider ongoing website maintenance.
  • Consider better hosting: our guide to moving hosts covers it. Start with the Start Here hub if you are rebuilding your setup.

FAQ

What should I do first if my WordPress site is hacked?

Call your host, put the site in maintenance mode, and save a copy of the files, database and logs before changing anything. Then change all passwords and scan.

Can I fix a hacked website myself?

Sometimes. If you have a clean backup and can restore it and update everything, yes. Finding backdoors is harder; if the site is reinfected or client data may be involved, bring in a professional.

How long does Google take to remove the hacked warning?

Google says most reviews take several days or weeks. You get emails when it is received and when it finishes. Resubmitting while pending is discouraged.

Is a free scanner enough to confirm my site is clean?

No. Remote scanners such as Sucuri SiteCheck cannot see server-side files and say they do not detect backdoors. Use a plugin scan and a manual check too.

Do I have to tell clients my website was hacked?

It depends on whether client confidential information was compromised and on your state’s rules. ABA Formal Opinion 483 discusses notice duties. Get advice from your state bar or ethics counsel.

Will a backup restore remove the hack?

Only if the backup predates the infection. Even then, update everything and change passwords, or the same weakness is used again.

Conclusion: your next steps

Today: call your host, switch to maintenance mode, copy the site, and reset all access. This week: scan, restore or clean, update, then request Google review. After that: add a firewall, backups and a maintenance routine, and decide with your ethics counsel whether any notice is needed.

Options: your host (some include cleanup), a malware-removal service such as Sucuri (see our tool comparisons hub), or a WordPress developer. Ask what is included, how long it takes, and whether they will explain how the attacker got in.

How do I get Google to remove the hacked warning?

Fix everything first, then request a review in Search Console. Google’s Security Issues report covers three categories: hacked content, malware and unwanted software, and social engineering. If you have not set up Search Console, our GA4 and Search Console setup guide walks through it. You will need verified ownership to see the report.

  1. Open the Security Issues report and expand each issue. Use the sample URLs to find the problem; the list is a sample, not necessarily complete.
  2. Fix the issue across the whole site and fix every issue listed. Google says fixing only some pages will not earn a partial return to search results.
  3. Test your fixes, and make sure the pages are not blocked from Google by login, robots.txt or noindex.
  4. Select Request Review. Explain the issue, the steps you took and the outcome.
  5. Wait. Google says most reviews take several days or weeks, with emails when the request is received and completed. Do not resubmit while pending.

Sources: Security Issues report and Manual Actions report help pages. Other blocklists (Bing, antivirus vendors) have their own removal processes; WordPress.org recommends registering with the major webmaster consoles.

Could my contact form or intake data have been exposed?

Possibly, and for a law firm this is the question that matters most. Check where form submissions go. Some plugins store entries in the WordPress database, which an attacker with admin or database access could read. Others only email you. Review: stored form entries, uploaded files in the media library, user accounts, and any email or CRM integrations whose keys sit in the site settings. If entries were stored, assume they could have been read and note what they contained. Afterward, follow our guide to a secure contact form for a law firm website and avoid storing sensitive details on the site at all.

What are a lawyer’s ethics duties after a website hack?

This is general information, not legal advice. Check with your state bar or ethics counsel. ABA Formal Opinion 483 (October 2018), “Lawyers’ Obligations After an Electronic Data Breach or Cyberattack,” addresses what lawyers should do when client confidential information may be compromised. As summarized by secondary sources (the ABA site blocked our automated access, so we could not read the opinion itself), it points to these duties:

  • Monitor so a breach is detected, which is part of a firm having reasonable security.
  • Act promptly to stop the breach and limit the damage, then restore systems.
  • Make reasonable efforts to determine what occurred: what was accessed and whose information it was.
  • Consider notifying clients when material client confidential information was compromised, tied to the duty to keep clients informed.

A marketing site with no client data is a different situation from one holding stored intake forms. Keep your incident notes: what you found, when, and what you did. They support any decision on notice.

How do I prevent it from happening again?

  • Put a web application firewall (WAF) in front of the site. See Cloudflare for law firm websites or a security plugin comparison.
  • Keep WordPress, themes and plugins updated and remove unused ones.
  • Use 2FA and unique passwords; give each person their own login.
  • Run automatic offsite backups and test a restore.
  • Work through the law firm website security checklist and consider ongoing website maintenance.
  • Consider better hosting: our guide to moving hosts covers it. Start with the Start Here hub if you are rebuilding your setup.

FAQ

What should I do first if my WordPress site is hacked?

Call your host, put the site in maintenance mode, and save a copy of the files, database and logs before changing anything. Then change all passwords and scan.

Can I fix a hacked website myself?

Sometimes. If you have a clean backup and can restore it and update everything, yes. Finding backdoors is harder; if the site is reinfected or client data may be involved, bring in a professional.

How long does Google take to remove the hacked warning?

Google says most reviews take several days or weeks. You get emails when it is received and when it finishes. Resubmitting while pending is discouraged.

Is a free scanner enough to confirm my site is clean?

No. Remote scanners such as Sucuri SiteCheck cannot see server-side files and say they do not detect backdoors. Use a plugin scan and a manual check too.

Do I have to tell clients my website was hacked?

It depends on whether client confidential information was compromised and on your state’s rules. ABA Formal Opinion 483 discusses notice duties. Get advice from your state bar or ethics counsel.

Will a backup restore remove the hack?

Only if the backup predates the infection. Even then, update everything and change passwords, or the same weakness is used again.

Conclusion: your next steps

Today: call your host, switch to maintenance mode, copy the site, and reset all access. This week: scan, restore or clean, update, then request Google review. After that: add a firewall, backups and a maintenance routine, and decide with your ethics counsel whether any notice is needed.

title.rendered: Sucuri Review for Law Firms (2026): Website Firewall and Malware Cleanup

content.raw:
Quick answer: This Sucuri review covers a cloud website firewall plus monitoring and hands-on malware cleanup that you can add to any website, including WordPress. As of November 2026, Sucuri's platform plans for one site are listed at $229, $339 and $549 per year. Sucuri is worth considering if your host offers no firewall or cleanup help, or if you want one team to clean a hacked site and clear blocklists. If your managed host already covers those, the free Sucuri plugin and scanner may be all you need.

Sucuri is part of GoDaddy: its terms of service name the company as GoDaddy Media Temple, Inc. d/b/a Sucuri, a subsidiary of GoDaddy Operating Company, LLC. This guide explains what you get, how the firewall works, what it costs, and what to weigh before you change your DNS. For a side-by-side with other tools, see our WordPress security plugins comparison for law firms.

What is Sucuri and what does it do for a law firm website?

Sucuri sells website security as a service. Its main product, the Website Security Platform, bundles four things: a cloud-based web application firewall (WAF), scheduled malware and blocklist monitoring, unlimited manual malware removal, and a content delivery network (CDN). It is platform-agnostic, so it works with WordPress, other content management systems and custom sites, according to Sucuri's plan comparison.

For a small law firm, the appeal is simple. Your site is your storefront, and a hacked site that redirects visitors to spam or gets flagged as unsafe costs trust. Sucuri aims to stop attacks before they reach your host and to clean up if something gets through. It does not remove the need for updates, backups and good passwords. Our law firm website security checklist covers those basics.

How does the Sucuri website firewall work?

It is a reverse proxy. Per Sucuri's activation steps, you add your site to the firewall, then enable protection by changing your DNS records. Once active, the firewall "intercepts and inspects all incoming packets" so that only safe requests reach your server. Sucuri says it creates SSL certificates for the firewall servers automatically, and that Professional or Business plans can upload a custom certificate.

Because traffic now flows through Sucuri, two practical points follow:

  • DNS access matters. You (or whoever manages your domain) must be able to edit DNS records. If your domain is at GoDaddy, our guide to registering a law firm domain at GoDaddy explains where DNS lives.
  • Lock down the origin. If attackers learn your host's real IP address they may bypass the firewall. Ask Sucuri support or your host how to restrict the server to firewall traffic only.
  • Visitor data passes through it. Sucuri's terms say the firewall service may collect IP addresses and request URLs, and that HTTP traffic may contain data fields users complete. That can include contact-form entries.

That last point is a confidentiality consideration, not a reason to avoid the tool. ABA Formal Opinion 477 says lawyers must make reasonable efforts to secure client information in transit, with the level of care depending on the sensitivity of the information (ABA Formal Opinion 477). Read the provider terms, avoid collecting sensitive details in web forms, and check your state bar's guidance. See also our guide to a secure contact form for a law firm website.

Does Sucuri stop DDoS attacks?

Sucuri lists DDoS mitigation as part of the firewall and says its Anycast network can mitigate large attacks, including layer 3, 4 and 7 attacks (plan comparison). Its page also lists a "currently under attack" option during setup. We cannot verify attack-size limits, so ask Sucuri what applies to your plan if DDoS is your main worry. For most small firms, a DDoS attack is a rarer risk than a compromised plugin or stolen password.

Does Sucuri scan for malware remotely or on the server?

Both, depending on what you use. The free SiteCheck scanner is remote: it only sees what a browser sees, so Sucuri says it will not detect anything on the server side. It checks for known malware, blocklist status, out-of-date software and similar issues, and Sucuri notes remote scanners have limited access and results are not guaranteed.

Paid platform plans add a server-side scanner. Sucuri's terms of service describe a "Website Server Side Scanner that checks your website files for security issues that might be missed by a remote scan," alongside SEO spam scanning, blocklist notifications, uptime, DNS and SSL change alerts. Scan frequency depends on the plan (see the table below).

How much does Sucuri cost in 2026?

As of November 2026, Sucuri's pricing page lists these prices, each covering one site. Prices change, so confirm on the page before you buy.

  • Sucuri also lists a Junior Dev plan ($999.98/year, for 2 to 5 sites) and custom multi-site pricing. Those are aimed at agencies and developers, not a single law firm site.
  • The SLA is an estimate of ticket response time. Sucuri states that resolution time varies with complexity and queue volume.
  • The plans list SSL support; only the Pro and Business plans can be preloaded with your existing purchased SSL certificate.
  • Services renew automatically at the then-current rate, which may be higher or lower, per the terms. Put the renewal date on your calendar.
  • A 30-day cancellation window applies, with a refund of the subscription fee if you have not submitted a malware removal request in that period (per the terms).

What does "unlimited malware removal" include?

Sucuri lists unlimited manual cleanups on every platform plan, with removal of backdoors and "blocklist warning removal," where the team requests removal of your site from blocklists on your behalf (plan comparison). It also lists quarantined backups of files touched during cleanup and a post-cleanup report with recommendations.

Read the fine print. The terms promise "reasonable commercial efforts" to clean an infected site, and if Sucuri cannot clean it, the sole remedy is a refund of the annual fee. The terms also say Sucuri does not warrant that the service will prevent infection or re-infection. Cleanup is not a guarantee against being hacked again, so you still need to fix how the attacker got in. If that has already happened to you, start with our guide on what to do if your law firm website is hacked.

Is the free Sucuri plugin enough?

The Sucuri Security plugin is free for all WordPress users, and you do not need a paid subscription to use it, according to the terms. Sucuri lists security activity auditing, file integrity monitoring, remote malware scanning, blocklist monitoring, hardening and post-hack actions. The plugin's WordPress.org page shows it is widely installed (600,000+ active installations at the time we looked).

The plugin does not include the firewall. Sucuri says connecting the firewall through the plugin is only available to customers on a platform plan. Think of the free plugin as a monitoring and audit-log tool, and the paid plans as the firewall and cleanup service. Do not run two full security plugins that overlap; our security plugin comparison explains how to layer them.

What are the pros and cons of Sucuri?

Pros

  • Cleanup help is included: unlimited manual removals and blocklist removal requests on platform plans.
  • Works with any CMS or host, because it sits in front of the site rather than inside it.
  • Firewall, DDoS protection and CDN are bundled; no separate CDN account to manage.
  • A free scanner and a free plugin let you try the tools before paying.
  • Published, itemized pricing for the single-site plans.

Cons

  • It needs a DNS change, and a mistake there can take your site or email offline. Get help if you are unsure.
  • Visitor traffic is routed through a third party, which deserves a look at the terms.
  • Renewal pricing can change, and billing is automatic.
  • The cleanup remedy is limited to refunds if Sucuri cannot clean the site, and there is no guarantee against re-infection.
  • Support is ticket-based on the single-site plans, so do not expect a phone-in-the-moment experience. Check Sucuri's page for current support options.
  • Overlap: if your host or Cloudflare already filters traffic, you may be paying twice for similar protection.

Do you still need Sucuri if your host has security?

Often, partly. Good managed WordPress hosts typically include server-level firewalls, malware scanning, backups and sometimes cleanup. Compare what your host lists before buying. Ask these questions:

  1. Is there a web application firewall, and who maintains the rules?
  2. Is malware cleanup included, or billed per incident?
  3. Who requests blocklist removal if Google flags the site?
  4. Are backups stored off the server, and have you tested a restore?

Our hosting guides show what several providers include, such as the Hostinger review and the SiteGround review. If the answers cover you, skip the paid plan. If you already put your site behind Cloudflare, read our Cloudflare for law firm websites guide first, since stacking two proxies adds complexity.

How do you set up Sucuri on a WordPress site?

At a high level, based on Sucuri's activation steps:

  1. Buy a plan and add your domain in the Sucuri dashboard.
  2. Sucuri shows the DNS records to use. Note your current DNS settings first, including email (MX) records, so you can roll back.
  3. Choose SSL and caching options. If your site is under attack, Sucuri provides an "I am currently under attack" setting.
  4. Change the DNS record as instructed. Changes can take time to spread.
  5. Lock the origin server so only the firewall can reach it, and restrict admin access if possible.
  6. Test the site, the contact form and email delivery. Keep your normal website maintenance routine going: updates and backups still matter.

If you also want Sucuri's free plugin, install it from the WordPress plugin directory and generate the free API key so audit logs are stored off-site.

Who should (and should not) buy Sucuri?

  • Worth a look: firms whose host offers little security, firms that have been hacked, or firms that want a single vendor for firewall plus cleanup.
  • Probably not needed yet: firms on a managed host with firewall, scanning and free cleanup, especially if they already use a proxy like Cloudflare.
  • Start free: run SiteCheck on your site today, then decide.

For the wider picture of hardening a firm website, use the tool comparisons hub or our Start Here page. Passwords and 2FA protect the admin login that a firewall cannot; see our 1Password review.

FAQ

Is Sucuri owned by GoDaddy?

Yes. Sucuri's terms of service identify the company as GoDaddy Media Temple, Inc. d/b/a Sucuri, a subsidiary of GoDaddy Operating Company, LLC. You do not need to host or register your domain at GoDaddy to use it; the plans are described as platform-agnostic.

How much is Sucuri per year?

As of November 2026, Sucuri lists $229, $339 and $549 per year for its Basic, Pro and Business platform plans (one site each), plus firewall-only plans at $9.99 and $19.98 per month. Confirm on Sucuri's pricing page.

Is the Sucuri SiteCheck scanner free?

Yes, SiteCheck is a free remote scanner. It checks what is visible from outside, so it cannot see server-side files. Treat a clean result as a useful signal, not proof of safety.

Does Sucuri work with WordPress?

Yes. It works with WordPress and other platforms. For WordPress there is also a free plugin for audit logs, integrity checks and hardening, as described on Sucuri's plugin page.

Does Sucuri remove Google blocklist warnings?

Sucuri lists blocklist warning removal on its platform plans, meaning it requests removal on your behalf. Outcomes depend on the blocklist authority, so check the plan details.

Is a cloud firewall safe for client confidentiality?

It can be, if you understand that traffic passes through the provider. Review the terms, minimize sensitive data in web forms, and check your state bar guidance. This is general information, not legal advice.

Conclusion: next steps

  1. Run the free SiteCheck scan on your site and note any warnings.
  2. List what your host already includes (firewall, scanning, cleanup, backups).
  3. If gaps remain, compare Sucuri with the options in our security plugin guide.
  4. Before any DNS change, record current settings, including email records.

title.raw: How to Set Up 1Password for a Small Law Firm: Vaults, Sharing and Offboarding (2026)
title.rendered: How to Set Up 1Password for a Small Law Firm: Vaults, Sharing and Offboarding (2026)

content.raw:
Quick answer: to set up 1Password for business, start a free trial of a business plan, make two people Owners, save each Emergency Kit offline, create a few shared vaults, give those vaults to groups (not individuals), invite staff, turn on required two-factor authentication, and write down how you will offboard people. Most small firms can do this in about 30 days without disrupting anyone. The plan names and steps below come from 1Password's own support pages.

This guide is a practical rollout for a firm of roughly two to ten people. If you are still deciding whether 1Password is the right tool, read our 1Password review for law firms and our broader password manager guide for law firms first.

Which 1Password plan should a small law firm choose?

For shared firm logins you need a business plan, not a personal one. As of November 2026, 1Password's business pricing page lists two options, billed yearly:

Both offer a 14-day free trial with no credit card required. Extra Starter Pack seats are listed at $4.99 per seat per month. Prices change, so confirm on the pricing page before you buy.

Which one fits? A firm of three to nine people is usually fine on the Starter Pack for the core needs in this guide. Two things to check first. The groups documentation says custom groups are a Business feature, and the 2FA and permission screens described below are documented for Business. If you want custom groups such as "Attorneys" and "Staff", price the Business plan, and ask 1Password support which controls your specific plan includes before you commit.

How do I create the account and choose owners and admins?

Start the trial from the business pricing page and sign up with a firm email address. The account creator automatically becomes an Owner. According to the groups page, Owners can do everything Administrators can, plus change billing and delete the team. Administrators can manage vaults, groups and people and can recover accounts. Team Members have no team-level administrative permissions.

A sensible small-firm setup:

  • Two Owners. The managing attorney and one trusted backup (a partner or office manager). The groups page notes there must be at least one Owner, but a single Owner is a single point of failure.
  • One or two Administrators if you have an office manager who handles staff changes.
  • Everyone else as a Team Member. Fewer admins means fewer people who can see everything.

1Password also advises that at least two people have recovery permission so someone can help if a recovering person is locked out (recovery guide). Two Owners satisfies that.

What do I do with the Emergency Kit?

Each person gets an Emergency Kit PDF when they create their account. Per 1Password, it holds your sign-in address, email, Secret Key and a Setup Code QR, plus a blank line to write your account password. It does not contain your password. 1Password suggests printing a copy and keeping it somewhere safe, such as a safe deposit box. For a law firm, keep the printed kits in a locked cabinet or safe, not in a shared folder or in email. Note that if your administrator turns Emergency Kits off, or you sign in with SSO, you cannot save one.

What vault structure works for a law firm?

A vault is a container of logins that you share with chosen people or groups. There is no single right layout, and the one below is illustrative. The principle: split by who needs the access, not by software brand.

Two cautions. First, trust-account and banking credentials deserve the tightest vault; many firms keep it to Owners only. Second, check your court's and your bank's rules before you share any login. Some courts require individual e-filing credentials per attorney, and sharing those may violate their terms. When in doubt, ask the court clerk. For the ethics background on securing client information, check the ABA model rules on confidentiality and your state bar's guidance.

Everyone also has a built-in Employee vault that cannot be renamed or deleted. Treat it as private working space, and tell staff that firm credentials belong in the shared vaults so they are still there when someone leaves.

How do groups and permissions work?

The vault sharing page explains that you share a vault with a group via Vaults, then People or Groups, then Manage. On Business, permissions include View Items, Create Items, Edit Items, Archive Items and Delete Items, plus a separate Manage Vault permission that controls access and deletion but does not by itself let you view or edit items. Business also has client settings such as View and Copy Passwords, Export Items, Print Items and Copy and Share Items. On Teams plans the choices are simpler: Allow Viewing, Allow Editing and Allow Managing.

Practical rules:

  1. Share vaults with groups, so adding a new paralegal is one click.
  2. Give "view and copy" to people who only need to log in; reserve edit rights for the few who maintain the logins.
  3. Remove export and print rights from the groups that do not need them.
  4. If you remove someone from a vault but they still have access, check whether a group still grants it.

How do I invite staff and import existing passwords?

Per the team member guide, you can invite by email, share a sign-up link restricted to your allowed email domains, or (for smaller teams) invite through Slack. Email invitations expire after five days and can be resent. Sign-up links do not expire until you revoke them, so treat the link like a password and revoke it after onboarding.

For importing, the import guide lists Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave and Safari plus other password managers such as LastPass, Bitwarden, Dashlane and KeePass. CSV files can bring in logins, credit cards and secure notes through 1Password.com. If you cannot create vaults, you can only import into your own Employee-type vault.

A clean way to migrate:

  1. Have each person export their browser passwords to a file and import them into their own Employee vault.
  2. For shared firm logins in a spreadsheet, import the CSV once, then move items into the right shared vault.
  3. Delete the exported file, empty the trash, and then remove saved passwords from the browser. 1Password's page does not cover this step, but an exported plain-text file is the riskiest thing in the whole project.

How do I require two-factor authentication?

Owners, administrators, or members of a group with the Manage Settings permission can do it. Per the 2FA management page:

  1. Sign in at 1Password.com and choose Policies in the sidebar.
  2. Select Manage on the Authentication policy.
  3. First set the account password policy to Strict requirements. 1Password says you cannot enforce 2FA until this is done.
  4. Turn on Enforce two-factor authentication.

Members are prompted to set it up when they sign up, sign in on a new device, or next unlock 1Password. You can allow security keys, use Duo, and create a team report to see who has turned it on. Also turn on 2FA for your email, domain registrar and website admin accounts, since those are what an attacker wants. Our law firm website security checklist covers the website side.

How do I share a password with an outside vendor or accountant?

You have two options.

  • Guest account. Per the guest accounts page, a guest has no Employee vault and can access only one vault that an Owner or Administrator chooses. Invite from Invitations, choose Invite by Email, then Guest as the user type; the guest must accept and be confirmed before you share a vault with them. Teams includes 5 guests and Business 20; extra guests cost more. This suits an ongoing web developer or IT provider, who gets just the "IT / Website" vault.
  • Item sharing link. For one-off sharing, the item sharing page says you copy a link with an expiry you choose; if you enter the recipient's email, they must verify it first. Business admins can manage sharing settings and stop links from the audit log.

When a guest leaves, remove them and change the passwords they could see. 1Password notes guests may have copied items before removal.

What happens when someone forgets their password?

For a business account, the recovery route is an administrator. Per the recovery guide:

  1. An Owner or Administrator opens People, picks the person and selects Begin Recovery.
  2. The person gets an email, confirms their address, and sets a new Secret Key and account password.
  3. The admin receives an email and selects Complete Recovery.

Afterward the person keeps access to their vaults, must sign in again on all devices, must save a new Emergency Kit, and their two-factor authentication is reset. Because recovery relies on email, verify the request by phone or in person before approving it. 1Password's own guidance on verifying identity is thin, so set a firm rule. The recovery codes page describes codes for individual and family accounts only; business accounts rely on administrators, which is why a second Owner matters.

How do I offboard a departing employee?

1Password's offboarding guide gives this order:

  1. Move data. Have the person move work items from their Employee vault to a shared firm vault. 1Password warns not to delete the account until they have, and a Business Watchtower report can confirm the vault is empty.
  2. Suspend. Go to People, select the person, More Actions, Suspend. It is reversible with Reactivate.
  3. Change shared passwords. Review the vaults they could access. If they were an Owner or Administrator, assume they could reach every password in the vaults they managed. Change each affected password, starting with banking, email, registrar and website admin.
  4. Delete the account. This is permanent, and the Employee vault items are not recoverable.

One caveat from the team member guide: if the person is offline when you suspend or delete them, their items stay accessible until they next unlock 1Password while online. So rotate critical passwords quickly. Also remove them from systems 1Password does not control, such as email, case management and the website. If a departure involves suspected misuse, see what to do if your law firm website is hacked.

What is a realistic 30-day rollout?

  • Days 1-7: Start the trial, pick the plan, create the account, add a second Owner, store Emergency Kits, set the strict password policy.
  • Days 8-14: Create groups and vaults, move shared logins in, set permissions.
  • Days 15-21: Invite staff, run imports, enforce 2FA, hold a 20-minute training.
  • Days 22-30: Add guests for vendors, test a recovery with a spare account, write a one-page offboarding checklist, delete old exports and browser-saved passwords.

After 30 days, schedule a quarterly review of who is in each group. Website logins also belong in your regular maintenance routine; see our law firm website maintenance guide and WordPress security plugin comparison.

FAQ

How much does 1Password for business cost?

As of November 2026, the pricing page lists Teams Starter Pack at $24.95 per month for 10 users and Business at $8.99 per user per month, both billed yearly. Both have a 14-day free trial.

Can a law firm share one 1Password login among staff?

Yes, through shared vaults. Check the rules of the site first; some courts and banks require individual credentials.

What if the only Owner loses their password?

Recovery needs an administrator or owner, so a sole admin can be locked out. Keep two Owners and store Emergency Kits safely.

Does suspending an employee lock them out immediately?

Not necessarily. 1Password says offline members keep access until they next unlock while connected to the internet, so change critical passwords promptly.

Can I require 2FA for everyone?

Yes, from Policies, Authentication policy, after setting the password policy to Strict requirements.

Where do I start?

With the trial, two Owners and one shared vault. Add the rest in stages.

Conclusion: next steps

Start the 14-day trial, add a second Owner, and build only three vaults at first. Enforce 2FA before inviting everyone, and write your offboarding checklist before you need it. For the buying decision see the 1Password review, and for the bigger picture visit Start Here or our tool comparisons.

title.raw: 1Password Review for Law Firms (2026): Teams vs Business
title.rendered: 1Password Review for Law Firms (2026): Teams vs Business

content.raw:
This article is general information, not legal advice.

Quick answer: this 1Password review for law firms comes down to one choice. Teams Starter Pack suits a firm of up to 10 people that just needs shared vaults at a flat price. 1Password Business suits firms that want single sign-on, admin reports, more guest accounts and managed Travel Mode. Both use the same Secret Key plus account password design and end-to-end encryption.

Prices below are as of November 2026 from 1Password's business pricing page. Confirm them before you buy, because vendors change plans often.

Key takeaways

  • Teams Starter Pack: $24.95 per month flat for up to 10 members, billed yearly ($299.40 per year). Business: $8.99 per user per month, billed yearly.
  • SSO unlock (Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta and others) is a Business feature, per 1Password's support pages.
  • Each account needs a password you remember and a Secret Key you must store safely. Plan for lost-access recovery on day one.
  • A password manager helps show "reasonable efforts" under ABA Model Rule 1.6(c), but it does not replace a security policy.

Is 1Password good for law firms?

For most small firms, yes, on the merits of its design. 1Password uses two secrets to protect an account, and its security page says the company cannot see what you save. It also holds SOC 2 Type 2 certification and publishes information on independent assessments. Those are reasons to put it on a shortlist. They are not a guarantee, and no tool removes the need for good habits such as unique passwords and multi-factor authentication.

This page is a deep review of one product. For a side-by-side with other options, see our password manager comparison for law firms. For step-by-step rollout, see how to set up 1Password for a law firm.

How we compared

We have not run 1Password inside a firm for this review. The comparison is based on 1Password's official pricing, security and support pages, which we opened in November 2026. We give no ratings or scores. Where a page did not say, we say so.

What does 1Password cost for a law firm?

Both paid tiers offer a 14-day free trial with no credit card, according to the pricing page. Payment options listed include credit card, ACH direct debit for eligible US bank accounts and gift cards. One caution: the Teams headline on the page shows a per-user figure that does not obviously match the flat $24.95 in the FAQ. Treat the flat monthly figure as the one to verify with 1Password before budgeting.

Math example for a 6-person firm: Teams Starter Pack is $299.40 per year at the listed flat rate. Business at $8.99 per user would be 6 × $107.88 = $647.28 per year. Business costs more, so it needs to earn its keep through SSO, reports or guests.

How does the Secret Key security model work?

Your 1Password account is protected by an account password only you know and a 128-bit Secret Key, per the 1Password security page. The page describes a dual-key model and says 1Password cannot see what you have saved. It also says the service uses Secure Remote Password so credentials are not sent across the internet to sign in.

In plain terms: someone who steals your password still lacks the Secret Key, and someone who gets the encrypted data from 1Password's servers cannot open it with the password alone. The trade-off is that you must keep the Secret Key (often saved in an Emergency Kit) somewhere safe.

Has 1Password been audited?

1Password states it is SOC 2 Type 2 certified, and the report can be requested. Its security assessments page also lists ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 27017:2015, 27018:2019 and 27701:2019, earlier penetration tests and code review by Independent Security Evaluators in 2020, an architecture assessment by Onica, and a HackerOne bug bounty. Newer penetration test reports are shared through the 1Password Trust Center. Ask for the SOC 2 report if your clients or insurer request vendor evidence.

How do shared vaults and permissions work?

A vault is a container of logins and notes. Instead of passing passwords by email or chat, a firm puts them in a shared vault, for example "Billing", "Court e-filing" or "Marketing accounts", and grants access to people or groups. 1Password says Business includes expanded role-based vault sharing and permissions compared with Teams Starter Pack. We could not open the detailed permission-level page, so check 1Password's support site for the exact levels each plan offers.

A practical pattern for a small firm: one vault per function, not per person, and staff added by group so departures need one change.

Does 1Password support guest accounts for outside people?

Yes. The pricing page lists 5 guest accounts on Teams Starter Pack and 20 on Business. Guests are useful for a bookkeeper, an IT contractor or a marketing vendor who needs a single vault. Share only the vault they need, and remove them when the engagement ends. Avoid sharing client-confidential passwords with outsiders unless your engagement terms cover it.

What does Watchtower do?

Watchtower flags compromised sites, passwords exposed in a data breach, reused and weak passwords, unsecured http logins, sites where passkeys or two-factor codes are available but not saved, and expiring items, per 1Password's Watchtower page. For business accounts, admins can use Business Watchtower reports to track issues across items in shared vaults. That is a Business feature on the pricing page; Teams lists general security alerts only.

Does 1Password support passkeys and two-factor codes?

Yes. 1Password's plans list 2FA, biometrics and passkeys, and Watchtower prompts you to store one-time codes and passkeys where a site supports them. Our website team often points firms to the law firm website security checklist, where strong, unique admin passwords and 2FA are first-line items.

Which plan includes single sign-on?

1Password's Unlock with SSO page ties the feature to 1Password Business. Supported providers include Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, Duo, JumpCloud, OneLogin, Ping Identity, Auth0 and generic OIDC. If you run Microsoft 365 or Google, this matters: staff sign in with the identity they already use, and removing the account in your directory cuts access. See our guides to Microsoft 365 setup and Google Workspace setup for the identity side.

How do offboarding and account recovery work?

Per 1Password's recovery page, team administrators, owners and members of a custom group with the Recover Accounts permission can recover accounts for people who cannot sign in. The person gets a new Secret Key and password, regains vaults, and their two-factor authentication is reset. 1Password recommends at least two people have recovery ability.

For offboarding, the checklist is:

  1. Remove the person from groups and vaults, or suspend or remove the account from the admin console.
  2. Change shared credentials they could see, such as bank portals, e-filing and registrar logins. Removal does not erase anything a person has already seen or copied.
  3. Reassign any items kept only in their private vault.
  4. Record the date and what was changed in your file.
