title.rendered: How to Register a Law Firm Domain on GoDaddy (and Skip the Upsells) (2026)

content.raw:
Quick answer: To register a domain on GoDaddy, search for your firm name, pick a term, create an account in the firm's own name and email, decline the checkout extras you do not need, and then turn on auto-renew, 2-step verification and the transfer lock. Email protection, hosting and website builders are optional add-ons that most law firms can skip at checkout. The whole purchase takes about ten minutes; the DNS setup that follows is where mistakes happen.

Key takeaways

  • Register the domain in an account owned by the firm, with a firm-controlled email address, not a web designer's or an assistant's personal login.
  • At checkout, take the domain and (if offered for your extension) domain privacy. Skip bundled hosting, website builders and email unless you have decided to use them.
  • Turn on auto-renew, 2-step verification and the transfer lock on day one. An expired domain takes your website and email down together.
  • DNS is what connects the domain to your website (A or CNAME or nameservers) and your email (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC). Copy the exact values from your host and email provider.

This guide covers the GoDaddy purchase and settings. For a wider look at alternatives see our best domain registrars for law firms, and for a verdict on the company itself read our GoDaddy review for law firms. GoDaddy changes its screens often, so the steps below describe what to look for rather than exact button positions.

Quick pick

Choosing Google Workspace? Start through our referral link → and ask us for a 10% first-year promo code.

We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. It never changes our recommendations.

Step 1: What domain name should a law firm register?

Choose the name before you open GoDaddy. Short, easy to say aloud and easy to spell wins: the firm name, or lawyer surnames, with no hyphens or numbers. Say it over the phone to a colleague; if they have to ask how it is spelled, rethink it. Check that the matching name is not a trademark or firm name belonging to someone else, and check your state bar's rules on firm names and advertising, which vary by state.

Then decide on the extension. For most small firms .com remains the safe default because people type it automatically, while .law and .attorney can add clarity. We compare them in .law vs .com vs .attorney for law firms. If you can afford it, owning both your .com and one alternative and redirecting the second to the first is common.

Step 2: How do you search for and buy a domain on GoDaddy?

GoDaddy's domain search page shows whether a name is available and suggests alternatives. Pricing varies by extension and changes often, and GoDaddy's pages blocked our automated checks, so we are not quoting a price here: see GoDaddy's site for the current first-year and renewal price of your exact extension. Always compare the renewal price, not only the introductory first-year price.

  1. Type the name you want into the search box and check the exact result for your extension.
  2. If it is taken, try the lawyer-surname version or add the practice area or city (for example a surname plus "law" or "legal"). Avoid hyphens.
  3. Add the domain to your cart and review the term and any pre-selected extras.
  4. Create or sign in to a GoDaddy account in the firm's name (see Step 4 first).
  5. Pay with a firm card and keep the receipt for your records.

Step 3: How long should you register a domain for?

GoDaddy's help pages describe renewal terms from 1 to 10 years for the domains they cover, though the maximum depends on the extension. A longer term protects you against a missed renewal and avoids yearly price creep, but it ties up cash and does not replace auto-renew. A sensible middle path for most firms: register for one to three years, keep auto-renew on, and keep a card on file that does not expire soon. Registering a longer term is not a ranking factor you should count on, so choose on convenience and risk.

Step 4: Who should own the GoDaddy account?

The firm should own the account and the domain. This is the single most important decision in the whole process. Plenty of firms discover years later that the domain sits in a former web designer's account, an ex-employee's personal email, or a vendor's reseller login. Getting it back can be slow and stressful, and in the meantime you cannot change DNS or move the site.

  • Create the account with a firm-controlled mailbox such as an office manager or partner address that more than one person can reach, ideally on a different domain than the one being registered (otherwise a lapse locks you out of the recovery email).
  • Put the managing partner or firm as the registrant contact with accurate details.
  • Do not share one password. If a web developer or IT person needs access, use GoDaddy's delegate access, which lets another person use products in your account without your password; the owner must accept the invitation.
  • Store the login and recovery codes in a shared password manager the partners control. Our siblings on this topic: 1Password review and how to set up 1Password for a law firm.

Step 5: Which checkout add-ons are worth buying?

GoDaddy's cart often pre-selects or promotes extras. Here is how to think about them. Features and prices change, so confirm each on GoDaddy's checkout page.

GoDaddy also lists some protections as free: the transfer lock (GoDaddy says almost all domains come with it enabled by default), two-factor authentication on your account, and a DMARC record with a quarantine policy added automatically, per its domain security guide. Verify these on your own account rather than assuming.

Step 6: How do you turn on auto-renew, 2-step verification and the domain lock?

Do these three things the same day you buy.

  1. Auto-renew. In your domain settings, make sure renewal is set to automatic and the payment method is current. GoDaddy says it attempts to auto-renew on the expiration date, and that if the first billing attempt fails the domain is parked; redemption fees can apply about 12 days after expiry (GoDaddy help). Also put the expiry date in the partners' calendar.
  2. 2-step verification. Add a verification method first, then open your account's security page and switch 2-Step Verification on (GoDaddy help). GoDaddy's guide says codes can come by phone, email or an authenticator app; an authenticator app is the stronger choice over SMS.
  3. Domain lock. Open the domain's settings, find the Transfer section and confirm the lock is on (GoDaddy help). It prevents transfers to another registrar; you unlock it when you deliberately move the domain later. GoDaddy notes changes can take up to 90 minutes to show.

Step 7: How do you point a GoDaddy domain to your website host?

The domain and the website are separate things. The domain is the address; your host stores the site. You connect them with DNS (the internet's address book). There are two common ways, and your host's instructions will say which one to use:

  • Change the nameservers to your host's (or to a service such as Cloudflare). DNS is then managed at that provider, not GoDaddy.
  • Keep GoDaddy's nameservers and add or edit records (usually an A record for the root domain and a CNAME for "www") with values your host gives you.

To change nameservers, GoDaddy's steps are: open the domain's settings, choose DNS, then Nameservers, pick GoDaddy or custom nameservers, and save; you may be asked to verify your identity. GoDaddy says changes usually take effect within an hour but can take up to 48 hours, and warns that changing nameservers can interrupt website or email (GoDaddy help). Because DNS then lives at the new provider, copy your existing MX and TXT records first or your email may stop.

If you are replacing an existing site, follow our guide to moving a law firm website without downtime. Building on Hostinger? See how to build a law firm website on Hostinger. Using Cloudflare for DNS and protection is covered in Cloudflare for law firm websites.

Step 8: How do you add email records (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC)?

Email will not work on your domain until it has records telling the world where mail goes. Define the terms once: MX records say which servers receive your mail; SPF lists the servers allowed to send as you; DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing mail; DMARC tells receivers what to do when SPF/DKIM fail and where to send reports. Together they reduce spoofing and keep legitimate mail out of spam. Our law firm email setup guide explains why they matter for client confidentiality.

How to add an MX record in GoDaddy

GoDaddy's steps: open the domain, go to DNS, choose Add New Record, select MX, then fill Name (@ for the root domain), Priority (lower numbers are tried first), Value (the mail server) and TTL. Domains with Domain Protection require extra identity verification before saving, and most changes take effect within an hour but can take up to 48 hours (GoDaddy help). This only works while the domain uses GoDaddy nameservers.

Google Workspace

Google's current instructions use a single MX value, smtp.google.com, with priority 1, and tell you to delete other MX records on the domain; accounts created before 2023 may keep the older ASPMX values. Google says it can take up to 72 hours, and then you activate Gmail in the Admin console (Google: set up MX records). Full walkthrough: Google Workspace setup for law firms.

Microsoft 365

Microsoft's admin center shows the exact MX value for your tenant to copy, with priority typically 0 and TTL 3600. It also gives an SPF TXT record (v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all), an autodiscover CNAME, and two DKIM CNAME records (selector1 and selector2). If an SPF record already exists, merge into it: a domain should have one SPF record only (Microsoft Learn). See Microsoft 365 setup for law firms.

DMARC

Add DMARC after SPF and DKIM are working. A cautious start is a monitoring policy (p=none) with a reporting address, then tighten to quarantine or reject once reports show your legitimate mail passing. GoDaddy says it adds a quarantine DMARC record automatically on some domains, so look at what is already there before creating a second one; a domain should have a single DMARC record.

GoDaddy domain setup mistakes to avoid

  • Registering under a vendor's or employee's account.
  • Leaving auto-renew off, or a card that expires next month.
  • Changing nameservers without first copying MX and TXT records.
  • Leaving old MX records in place after switching email providers.
  • Creating two SPF records instead of merging into one.
  • Skipping 2-step verification on the account that controls your email.

FAQ

Can I register a domain on GoDaddy without buying hosting or email?

Yes. A domain is sold separately. You can buy only the domain, then connect it to any host and any email provider through DNS.

Do I need domain privacy?

It is a good idea for a firm because it hides personal contact details from the public WHOIS directory. GoDaddy says Domain Privacy is added automatically to eligible domains, but not all extensions qualify. Check your cart.

What happens if my domain expires?

Your website and email stop working. GoDaddy says it attempts auto-renewal on the expiration date, and redemption fees may apply about 12 days after expiry, so renew early rather than late.

How long does it take for a new domain to work?

Registration is quick. DNS changes usually take effect within an hour but GoDaddy says they can take up to 48 hours, and Google says MX changes can take up to 72 hours.

Can I move my domain later?

Yes. Renew it, unlock it, and start the transfer at the new registrar. GoDaddy notes domains registered or transferred in the last 60 days cannot be transferred.

Should the domain registrar also host my website?

Not necessarily. Keeping the domain at a registrar and the site at a specialist host makes either one easier to change. Compare options in our registrar guide.

Conclusion and next steps

  1. Pick the name and extension, then buy it in a firm-owned account.
  2. Decline extras you have not chosen; keep privacy.
  3. Turn on auto-renew, 2-step verification and the lock.
  4. Connect the website, then email, with MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
  5. Review our Start Here page for the next decision, or the website security checklist.

  • Create the account with a firm-controlled mailbox such as an office manager or partner address that more than one person can reach, ideally on a different domain than the one being registered (otherwise a lapse locks you out of the recovery email).
  • Put the managing partner or firm as the registrant contact with accurate details.
  • Do not share one password. If a web developer or IT person needs access, use GoDaddy’s delegate access, which lets another person use products in your account without your password; the owner must accept the invitation.
  • Store the login and recovery codes in a shared password manager the partners control. Our siblings on this topic: 1Password review and how to set up 1Password for a law firm.

Step 5: Which checkout add-ons are worth buying?

GoDaddy’s cart often pre-selects or promotes extras. Here is how to think about them. Features and prices change, so confirm each on GoDaddy’s checkout page.

GoDaddy also lists some protections as free: the transfer lock (GoDaddy says almost all domains come with it enabled by default), two-factor authentication on your account, and a DMARC record with a quarantine policy added automatically, per its domain security guide. Verify these on your own account rather than assuming.

Step 6: How do you turn on auto-renew, 2-step verification and the domain lock?

Do these three things the same day you buy.

  1. Auto-renew. In your domain settings, make sure renewal is set to automatic and the payment method is current. GoDaddy says it attempts to auto-renew on the expiration date, and that if the first billing attempt fails the domain is parked; redemption fees can apply about 12 days after expiry (GoDaddy help). Also put the expiry date in the partners’ calendar.
  2. 2-step verification. Add a verification method first, then open your account’s security page and switch 2-Step Verification on (GoDaddy help). GoDaddy’s guide says codes can come by phone, email or an authenticator app; an authenticator app is the stronger choice over SMS.
  3. Domain lock. Open the domain’s settings, find the Transfer section and confirm the lock is on (GoDaddy help). It prevents transfers to another registrar; you unlock it when you deliberately move the domain later. GoDaddy notes changes can take up to 90 minutes to show.

Step 7: How do you point a GoDaddy domain to your website host?

The domain and the website are separate things. The domain is the address; your host stores the site. You connect them with DNS (the internet’s address book). There are two common ways, and your host’s instructions will say which one to use:

  • Change the nameservers to your host’s (or to a service such as Cloudflare). DNS is then managed at that provider, not GoDaddy.
  • Keep GoDaddy’s nameservers and add or edit records (usually an A record for the root domain and a CNAME for “www”) with values your host gives you.

To change nameservers, GoDaddy’s steps are: open the domain’s settings, choose DNS, then Nameservers, pick GoDaddy or custom nameservers, and save; you may be asked to verify your identity. GoDaddy says changes usually take effect within an hour but can take up to 48 hours, and warns that changing nameservers can interrupt website or email (GoDaddy help). Because DNS then lives at the new provider, copy your existing MX and TXT records first or your email may stop.

If you are replacing an existing site, follow our guide to moving a law firm website without downtime. Building on Hostinger? See how to build a law firm website on Hostinger. Using Cloudflare for DNS and protection is covered in Cloudflare for law firm websites.

Step 8: How do you add email records (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC)?

Email will not work on your domain until it has records telling the world where mail goes. Define the terms once: MX records say which servers receive your mail; SPF lists the servers allowed to send as you; DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing mail; DMARC tells receivers what to do when SPF/DKIM fail and where to send reports. Together they reduce spoofing and keep legitimate mail out of spam. Our law firm email setup guide explains why they matter for client confidentiality.

How to add an MX record in GoDaddy

GoDaddy’s steps: open the domain, go to DNS, choose Add New Record, select MX, then fill Name (@ for the root domain), Priority (lower numbers are tried first), Value (the mail server) and TTL. Domains with Domain Protection require extra identity verification before saving, and most changes take effect within an hour but can take up to 48 hours (GoDaddy help). This only works while the domain uses GoDaddy nameservers.

Google Workspace

Google’s current instructions use a single MX value, smtp.google.com, with priority 1, and tell you to delete other MX records on the domain; accounts created before 2023 may keep the older ASPMX values. Google says it can take up to 72 hours, and then you activate Gmail in the Admin console (Google: set up MX records). Full walkthrough: Google Workspace setup for law firms.

Microsoft 365

Microsoft’s admin center shows the exact MX value for your tenant to copy, with priority typically 0 and TTL 3600. It also gives an SPF TXT record (v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all), an autodiscover CNAME, and two DKIM CNAME records (selector1 and selector2). If an SPF record already exists, merge into it: a domain should have one SPF record only (Microsoft Learn). See Microsoft 365 setup for law firms.

DMARC

Add DMARC after SPF and DKIM are working. A cautious start is a monitoring policy (p=none) with a reporting address, then tighten to quarantine or reject once reports show your legitimate mail passing. GoDaddy says it adds a quarantine DMARC record automatically on some domains, so look at what is already there before creating a second one; a domain should have a single DMARC record.

GoDaddy domain setup mistakes to avoid

  • Registering under a vendor’s or employee’s account.
  • Leaving auto-renew off, or a card that expires next month.
  • Changing nameservers without first copying MX and TXT records.
  • Leaving old MX records in place after switching email providers.
  • Creating two SPF records instead of merging into one.
  • Skipping 2-step verification on the account that controls your email.

FAQ

Can I register a domain on GoDaddy without buying hosting or email?

Yes. A domain is sold separately. You can buy only the domain, then connect it to any host and any email provider through DNS.

Do I need domain privacy?

It is a good idea for a firm because it hides personal contact details from the public WHOIS directory. GoDaddy says Domain Privacy is added automatically to eligible domains, but not all extensions qualify. Check your cart.

What happens if my domain expires?

Your website and email stop working. GoDaddy says it attempts auto-renewal on the expiration date, and redemption fees may apply about 12 days after expiry, so renew early rather than late.

How long does it take for a new domain to work?

Registration is quick. DNS changes usually take effect within an hour but GoDaddy says they can take up to 48 hours, and Google says MX changes can take up to 72 hours.

Can I move my domain later?

Yes. Renew it, unlock it, and start the transfer at the new registrar. GoDaddy notes domains registered or transferred in the last 60 days cannot be transferred.

Should the domain registrar also host my website?

Not necessarily. Keeping the domain at a registrar and the site at a specialist host makes either one easier to change. Compare options in our registrar guide.

Conclusion and next steps

  1. Pick the name and extension, then buy it in a firm-owned account.
  2. Decline extras you have not chosen; keep privacy.
  3. Turn on auto-renew, 2-step verification and the lock.
  4. Connect the website, then email, with MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
  5. Review our Start Here page for the next decision, or the website security checklist.

title.raw: GoDaddy Review for Law Firms (2026): Domains, Email and Website Builder
title.rendered: GoDaddy Review for Law Firms (2026): Domains, Email and Website Builder

content.raw:
Quick answer: This GoDaddy review comes down to convenience versus long-term cost. GoDaddy is a reasonable one-stop shop for a small law firm that wants a domain, Microsoft 365 email and a simple website under one login and one phone number. It is usually not the cheapest place to keep a domain or to renew services in year two, so check renewal prices before you buy and compare registrars in our best domain registrars for law firms guide.

Note on prices: GoDaddy's own pricing pages blocked our automated access when we wrote this, so we do not quote domain, email or hosting prices as facts. Where a number matters, we tell you to read it on GoDaddy's pricing pages and look for the renewal price.

Key takeaways

  • GoDaddy sells domains, Microsoft 365 email, a website builder (Airo AI builder) and WordPress hosting, so one account can cover a whole small-firm setup.
  • Promotional first-year prices and renewal prices are different numbers. Always compare the renewal line.
  • GoDaddy says domain privacy is on by default at no extra cost for eligible domains, so you should not need to buy it as a separate add-on for those.
  • Microsoft 365 bought through GoDaddy is managed in GoDaddy's panel. Buying direct from Microsoft gives you the full Microsoft admin center.
  • For a custom WordPress site, a dedicated host is often a better fit than a bundled plan.

How we compared GoDaddy

This review is based on GoDaddy and Microsoft documentation and help pages as of November 2026. We have not run hands-on tests, and we give no scores or ratings. GoDaddy's main product and pricing pages were not accessible to our tools, so plan prices are left for you to confirm on GoDaddy's site.

Is GoDaddy good for a small law firm?

It can be, if your priority is simplicity. One company handles the domain, the DNS records, the email and a basic site, and phone and chat support is attached to the same account. The tradeoffs are renewal pricing, add-on upsells at checkout and less control over bundled products. A firm that only needs a domain and email can do well here. A firm planning a custom WordPress site, or one that wants the lowest long-term cost, should shop around.

How much does a domain cost at GoDaddy?

GoDaddy advertises low first-year prices on many domains, and the renewal price is what you pay from year two onward. We could not open GoDaddy's live price list, so we do not publish .com, .law or .attorney prices here. On GoDaddy's domain search, look at the cart line that shows the renewal price, and confirm the term. Premium extensions such as .law and .attorney usually cost more than .com; our guide to .law vs .com vs .attorney explains which to pick.

Lowest long-term cost is where GoDaddy is most often beaten. If that is your main goal, compare registrars on renewal price in our registrar comparison. If you decide to register at GoDaddy, our step-by-step guide to registering a law firm domain at GoDaddy walks through the cart and settings.

Does GoDaddy include domain privacy?

For eligible domains, yes. GoDaddy's help page What is Domain Privacy? says privacy replaces your contact details in the public WHOIS directory with substitute details from its partner Domains By Proxy, and that it is on by default at no extra cost. ICANN requires registrars to collect your contact data, so GoDaddy keeps the real details on file. There are three levels: On (all hidden), Limited (shows organization, state and country) and Off (everything public). Many extensions, including .us, .ca, .de, .fr and .eu, are not eligible, and GoDaddy points to a separate Domain Protection product for those. Check your extension before assuming you are covered.

Should I buy Microsoft 365 email from GoDaddy or from Microsoft?

Buying direct from Microsoft is usually better if you expect to grow or want full control. Buying through GoDaddy is fine if you value a single bill and the simplest setup. When you buy through GoDaddy, it acts as a reseller and provides its own admin panel. A Microsoft Q&A answer describes users being sent back to the GoDaddy dashboard instead of the full Microsoft 365 admin center. That is a community reply, not official documentation, but it matches how resold tenants are described.

Moving later is possible but not trivial. GoDaddy's help page Move my Microsoft 365 email away from GoDaddy says the move transfers your whole tenant, that GoDaddy plans do not transfer so you buy new licenses from Microsoft or another reseller, that GoDaddy-sold add-ons such as Barracuda archiving, Proofpoint and ConnectWise backups are deleted in the move, and that once complete the organization cannot move back. It also warns not to buy new mailboxes elsewhere until the move finishes, or you will create a second tenant that cannot be merged.

Because law firms care about confidentiality, think about who administers your tenant, how multi-factor sign-in is enforced and whether you need archiving or encryption. Our Microsoft 365 setup guide for law firms covers the settings, law firm business email covers SPF, DKIM and DMARC, and Google Workspace vs Microsoft 365 helps you pick the platform first. Your domain can stay registered at GoDaddy while email lives at Microsoft, as long as the DNS records point correctly.

Is GoDaddy's Website Builder (Airo) good enough for a law firm?

For a simple brochure site, possibly. GoDaddy's Airo AI builder generates a site from a description of your business, and GoDaddy markets it with hosting and a custom domain included. Plan names, AI credit limits and prices have changed often, and the figures we found came from third-party summaries, so see GoDaddy's pricing page for current plans and whether the free domain applies after the first year.

Questions to ask before you commit: Can you export your content if you leave? Can you add the practice area pages, attorney bios, accessibility features and secure intake forms your firm needs? Does the plan show clear renewal pricing? Builders are fast to launch, but they limit customization and SEO control compared with WordPress. Our Squarespace vs WordPress vs Wix guide compares the trade-offs, and how much a law firm website costs puts the options in context.

What about GoDaddy WordPress hosting?

GoDaddy sells managed and shared WordPress hosting. We could not verify current plan prices, backups or security features from its pages, so confirm them directly on GoDaddy's hosting page and read the renewal terms. If your firm already uses GoDaddy for the domain and email, a bundled WordPress plan is convenient. If speed, staging and security matter most, compare dedicated WordPress hosts first: see our Hostinger review, SiteGround review and Kinsta review. You can host elsewhere and keep the domain at GoDaddy, and our guide to moving a site to a new host explains how.

What upsells should you watch for?

Add-ons are normal in any registrar cart, and GoDaddy is no exception. Treat each one as a separate buying decision.

  • Extra security or malware scanning that overlaps with a plugin or host protection you already have. See the website security checklist.
  • Paid SSL certificates when your host already provides one.
  • Extra backups or email archiving. Some firms genuinely need archiving; buy it deliberately.
  • Longer terms and auto-renew that lock in a price you have not compared.
  • Domain add-ons such as extra extensions or privacy for an extension that is already covered.

How good is GoDaddy support?

GoDaddy advertises phone and chat support, and that is a real attraction for lawyers who do not want to troubleshoot DNS. We have not tested the quality or hours, so we make no claim about them. Check the support options attached to the exact plan you buy. Also note that for Microsoft 365 bought through GoDaddy, GoDaddy is your first contact, and some issues may need escalation to Microsoft.

Who should choose GoDaddy, and who should look elsewhere?

How do I set up GoDaddy safely?

  1. Create the account with a firm-owned email and turn on two-factor authentication.
  2. Register or transfer the domain and confirm privacy is On if your extension is eligible.
  3. Write down the renewal price and date. Decide on auto-renew deliberately.
  4. Choose Microsoft 365 through GoDaddy or direct from Microsoft before you create mailboxes.
  5. Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC. See our email guide.
  6. Remove add-ons you did not choose.

Browse more side-by-side guides on our Tool Comparisons page, or start from Start Here.

FAQ

Is GoDaddy good for law firms?

It suits firms that want one vendor for domain, email and a basic site. It is less suited to firms that want the lowest renewal prices or a heavily customized WordPress site.

Does GoDaddy charge for domain privacy?

GoDaddy says privacy is on by default at no extra cost for eligible domains. Some extensions are not eligible, so check yours.

Is GoDaddy Microsoft 365 the same as Microsoft 365 from Microsoft?

It is Microsoft 365 resold by GoDaddy and managed in GoDaddy's panel. Buying direct gives full Microsoft admin control and Microsoft billing and support.

Can I move email from GoDaddy to Microsoft later?

Yes, but GoDaddy says the whole tenant moves, licenses do not transfer, some add-ons are deleted and you cannot move back.

Can I keep my domain at GoDaddy and host elsewhere?

Yes. Change the DNS records or nameservers to point at the new host or email provider.

What are GoDaddy's prices?

They change often and differ between first term and renewal. See GoDaddy's pricing pages and read the renewal line.

Conclusion and next steps

  • Decide whether you value one-stop convenience or lowest long-term cost.
  • If cost wins, read the registrar comparison first.
  • Choose email ownership (GoDaddy vs direct) before creating mailboxes.
  • Plan your website on a platform you can grow with.

title.rendered: Hostinger vs SiteGround for Law Firms: Which Budget Host Is Better? (2026)

content.raw:
Quick answer: In the Hostinger vs SiteGround matchup, Hostinger wins on price and SiteGround wins on support and features. Hostinger costs far less over three years. SiteGround offers 24/7 phone support, daily backups kept up to 30 days and staging on its GrowBig plan. For a simple law firm brochure site on a tight budget, choose Hostinger Unlimited. If you want a phone number to call and safer update testing, choose SiteGround GrowBig.

  • Cheapest over 3 years: Hostinger. The 48-month Unlimited prepay is $133.92 and covers the whole period (as of November 2026). SiteGround GrowBig costs $767.64 over the same three years at its 12-month terms.
  • Best support: SiteGround lists 24/7 chat, phone and ticket support. Hostinger lists 24/7 live chat only.
  • Best backups: SiteGround keeps up to 30 daily copies. Hostinger Unlimited keeps the last 7 days. Hostinger Premium needs a paid add-on for daily backups.
  • Both lose on email for client work. Included mailboxes are fine for a contact address. Use Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 for confidential client email.

If you or your web developer handle problems by chat and ticket anyway, it matters less.

Location does not by itself create a legal compliance advantage, and confidentiality duties turn on your own safeguards. Ask your state bar if you are unsure.

SiteGround lists free SSL, enhanced security, a Security Optimizer plugin and managed auto-updates for WordPress. Both are reasonable baselines. Neither replaces strong passwords, two-factor login, timely updates and tested backups.   4. Set up your own off-site backup in week one.

Neither wins for everyone. Hostinger is much cheaper over three years. SiteGround offers phone support, longer daily backup retention and staging on GrowBig. Pick Hostinger for cost, SiteGround for support.

Yes. Both advertise free migration help, and the site can stay live during the move. Your domain registration and email need separate handling.

We recommend matching the plan to your needs. We have not run speed or uptime tests on either host, so we make no performance claim.

title.rendered: How to Build a Law Firm Website on Hostinger (Step by Step, 2026)

content.raw:
Quick answer: To build a law firm website on Hostinger, buy a hosting plan (Unlimited is the usual pick for a firm because it includes daily backups), register your domain, install WordPress from hPanel, confirm SSL and backups, add four core pages (home, practice areas, attorney bios, contact), set up business email, lock down logins, and test before launch. A first version of a small firm site is realistic in a few days, if the content is ready.

This guide walks through each step in order. It assumes a solo lawyer or a small firm that wants a brochure-style site with a contact form, not an e-commerce store. For a verdict on whether Hostinger is a good host for firms at all, read our Hostinger review for law firms. Here we focus on doing the build.

Key takeaways

  • Hostinger plans and prices change often, and the headline price needs a 48-month prepayment. Check Hostinger's pricing page before you buy and budget for the renewal price.
  • Per Hostinger's plan page, Premium has weekly backups and Unlimited has daily backups. For a law firm, daily is the safer choice.
  • WordPress gives you the most control and the best long-term options. Hostinger's Website Builder is faster to start but harder to move away from.
  • The hard part is not installing WordPress. It is the content, the intake form, security and ongoing updates.
  • If nobody at the firm will handle updates and backups, choose managed hosting instead.

Should a law firm build on Hostinger WordPress or use Hostinger Website Builder?

Hostinger offers two ways to make a site. WordPress is the open-source content management system (CMS) that powers a large share of the web, and you install it on your hosting account. Hostinger Website Builder is Hostinger's own drag-and-drop tool with AI features and templates.

For most firms we recommend WordPress. It matches how law firm sites usually grow (more practice area pages, a blog, intake integrations). Our Squarespace vs WordPress vs Wix comparison covers the platform decision in more depth. The rest of this guide assumes WordPress.

Step 1: Which Hostinger plan should a law firm choose?

Hostinger's WordPress hosting page lists three main tiers. The figures below are the promotional terms shown there in November 2026, paid upfront for 48 months, excluding tax. Hostinger changes promotions frequently, so confirm everything on Hostinger's pricing page.

All three plans show a free domain for the first year and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Hostinger also notes that its "unlimited" features are subject to a Fair Usage Policy. Note that Hostinger's pages are not fully consistent on Premium's backup wording, so read the comparison table at checkout.

Which plan for which firm?

  • Premium: a solo lawyer with one simple site and a very tight budget, who is comfortable that backups run weekly.
  • Unlimited: most small firms. Daily backups matter if you add intake forms or publish often, and unlimited mailboxes cover staff addresses in year one.
  • Cloud Startup: only if the site has grown heavy (many pages, large media) or you want on-demand backups.

Two cost points to plan for: the low monthly price requires the long term, and the renewal rate is several times higher than the promo. Multiply the renewal monthly price by 12 when you build the firm's budget. For wider cost context, see how much a law firm website costs. If you are weighing Hostinger against other hosts, see our Hostinger vs SiteGround comparison.

Step 2: How do you choose and register the domain?

The domain is your web address and the base of your email addresses (for example, you@yourfirm.com). Hostinger's plans show a free domain for one year, after which it renews at the regular rate, so check the renewal price for your extension before you pick it.

  • Use the firm name or lawyer name. Avoid hyphens and numbers.
  • Compare extensions in our .law vs .com vs .attorney guide. Eligibility rules and renewal costs differ.
  • Register the domain in the firm's name with a firm-controlled email address, not a personal one that may disappear. See the best domain registrars for law firms if you prefer to keep the domain separate from hosting. Our GoDaddy domain walkthrough shows that route.

Keeping the domain at a separate registrar from the host is a common risk-reduction choice, since losing access to one account does not lock you out of both.

Step 3: How do you install WordPress with Hostinger hPanel?

hPanel is Hostinger's control panel. According to Hostinger's WordPress installation tutorial, there are two routes, and the menu names may change, so treat these as a guide.

Route A: the onboarding wizard (new plan)

  1. After purchase, follow the onboarding chat. On an existing plan, go to Websites, then Create site, then WordPress.
  2. Enter your domain and keep the suggested server region unless most visitors are elsewhere.
  3. Create the WordPress admin login: language, admin email and a strong administrator password.
  4. Choose "Build from scratch" for a blank site, or the AI option for a generated starter. For a law firm, we suggest blank; AI-generated placeholder text is easy to leave behind by mistake.

Route B: the WordPress installer (existing hosting site)

  1. In hPanel, open Websites, choose Manage site, then Website, then WordPress Install, and click Install.
  2. Enter the website title, administrator email, username and password. Do not use "admin" as the username.
  3. Under Advanced you can set an installation path. Leave "Create new database" selected.
  4. Hostinger's tutorial suggests updating only to minor versions automatically so security and bug-fix updates apply. Then click Install.

Hostinger warns that the installer overwrites existing files in the target site, so back up first if there is content you want to keep.

Step 4: Is SSL included, and what about backups?

SSL (the padlock and https:// in the address bar) encrypts traffic between a visitor and your site. Hostinger's tutorial says SSL activates automatically once your domain connects to the server, and that SSL and Force HTTPS are on by default. If you see a "connection is not private" warning right after launch, it is usually still being set up. Confirm the status on the hPanel dashboard and test every page, since mixed http/https content is a common leftover.

Backups are copies of your site you can restore after a mistake or hack. Per Hostinger's plan page, Premium backs up weekly and Unlimited and Cloud Startup daily. Set this up before you add content, and then:

  • Look at the Backups section in hPanel and note the schedule.
  • Do one test restore on a staging copy, or at least confirm you know where the restore button is.
  • Keep an independent off-site copy too. WordPress's own hardening guide advises regular backups of files and the database, with several past snapshots, and testing that you can restore them.

Step 5: What pages does a law firm website need?

A theme (the design layer) gives you the layout; the pages carry the value. Start with our list of WordPress themes for law firms. A fast, well-supported theme beats a flashy one. Then build these pages in this order:

  • Home: who you help, where, and one clear way to contact you.
  • Practice area pages: one page per service, not one page listing everything. See how to write practice area pages.
  • Attorney bio pages: credentials, bar admissions, approach. See how to write an attorney bio.
  • Contact / intake: phone, address, hours and a form. Keep the form minimal and avoid collecting confidential case details. See how to add a secure contact form.
  • Privacy policy and disclaimer: including a notice that sending a message does not create an attorney-client relationship, worded to your state bar's advertising rules. Ask your state bar or counsel what is required.

Also review accessibility from the start; our accessibility guide explains WCAG basics.

Step 6: How do you set up business email on Hostinger?

Hostinger plans show mailboxes for the first year (Premium: 2 per site; Unlimited and Cloud Startup: unlimited per site). Hostinger also sells standalone Business Email plans; its email hosting page lists Starter, Standard and Premium tiers with 5 GB, 20 GB and 50 GB per mailbox, and says the page does not state where data is stored. If client confidentiality or storage location matters to the firm, ask Hostinger directly.

Many firms prefer a dedicated email suite with stronger admin and compliance controls. Compare options in Google Workspace vs Microsoft 365 for law firms, and set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC using our business email guide. For sensitive client communications, see law firm email encryption.

Step 7: What security basics should you do on a new WordPress site?

Law firm sites hold contact details and are trusted by clients, so a hacked site is costly. The WordPress.org hardening guide lists the fundamentals:

  • Keep WordPress, themes and plugins updated; enable automatic updates where appropriate.
  • Use long, unique passwords from a password manager and turn on two-step authentication. Our password manager guide compares options.
  • Avoid common admin usernames like "admin".
  • Install only plugins you need and remove unused ones.
  • Back up and test restores.

Then add a security plugin and work through our law firm website security checklist. See WordPress security plugins for law firms, and our Sucuri review if you want a cloud firewall. If something goes wrong, read what to do if your law firm website is hacked.

Step 8: What should you check before launch?

Work through the checklist above, then test on a phone and a laptop, submit the form yourself, and confirm a human reads the inbox. Next, set up measurement with GA4 and Search Console, and claim your Google Business Profile. Our free website checklist and local SEO checklist cover what comes next. Speed matters too; see law firm website speed.

When should a law firm choose managed hosting instead of Hostinger?

Shared and cloud plans like Hostinger's give you a server and tools, but you remain responsible for the WordPress layer: updates, plugin choices, security and restores. Consider managed WordPress hosting if:

  • No one at the firm, or on retainer, will update and monitor the site.
  • You want the host to handle malware cleanup, staging and expert support.
  • The site generates enough business that downtime or a hack would cost more than the price gap.

See our Kinsta review, WP Engine review and the three-way comparison. Budget cost is only part of the picture; website maintenance takes time or money wherever you host. Browse more in our tool comparisons or start from Start Here.

FAQ

How long does it take to build a law firm website on Hostinger?

Installing WordPress takes minutes. Hostinger's tutorial says installation takes about two minutes. The real time goes into writing pages, collecting bios and photos, and testing, which commonly takes days to weeks.

Is Hostinger good for a law firm website?

It can be a good-value option for a simple brochure site if someone handles updates and backups. Our Hostinger review covers strengths and limits in detail.

Does Hostinger include a free domain and SSL?

Hostinger's plan pages show a free domain for the first year, and its tutorial says SSL and Force HTTPS are on by default once the domain connects. Renewal prices for the domain are separate; see Hostinger's pricing page.

Does Hostinger back up my WordPress site daily?

Per its plan page, Unlimited and Cloud Startup have daily backups, and Premium has weekly. Always confirm the current schedule in hPanel and keep an independent copy.

Can I use Hostinger Website Builder instead of WordPress?

Yes, and it is faster to start. The trade-off is less flexibility and a harder move later. Most firms planning to grow content and SEO choose WordPress.

How much will Hostinger cost after the first term?

As of November 2026, the page showed renewals of $10.99/mo (Premium), $16.99/mo (Unlimited) and $25.99/mo (Cloud Startup). Prices change, so check before you buy.

Conclusion: next steps

  • Decide WordPress vs builder (we suggest WordPress) and pick a plan, with Unlimited as the default.
  • Register the domain, install WordPress and confirm SSL and backups on day one.
  • Write the four core pages and a minimal intake form before launch.
  • Lock down logins and updates, then run the launch checklist.
  • If maintenance is not realistic in-house, price managed hosting or a maintenance service.

Quick answer: To build a law firm website on Hostinger, buy a hosting plan (Unlimited is the usual pick for a firm because it includes daily backups), register your domain, install WordPress from hPanel, confirm SSL and backups, add four core pages (home, practice areas, attorney bios, contact), set up business email, lock down logins, and test before launch. A first version of a small firm site is realistic in a few days, if the content is ready.

This guide walks through each step in order. It assumes a solo lawyer or a small firm that wants a brochure-style site with a contact form, not an e-commerce store. For a verdict on whether Hostinger is a good host for firms at all, read our Hostinger review for law firms. Here we focus on doing the build.

Key takeaways

  • Hostinger plans and prices change often, and the headline price needs a 48-month prepayment. Check Hostinger’s pricing page before you buy and budget for the renewal price.
  • Per Hostinger’s plan page, Premium has weekly backups and Unlimited has daily backups. For a law firm, daily is the safer choice.
  • WordPress gives you the most control and the best long-term options. Hostinger’s Website Builder is faster to start but harder to move away from.
  • The hard part is not installing WordPress. It is the content, the intake form, security and ongoing updates.
  • If nobody at the firm will handle updates and backups, choose managed hosting instead.

Should a law firm build on Hostinger WordPress or use Hostinger Website Builder?

Hostinger offers two ways to make a site. WordPress is the open-source content management system (CMS) that powers a large share of the web, and you install it on your hosting account. Hostinger Website Builder is Hostinger’s own drag-and-drop tool with AI features and templates.

For most firms we recommend WordPress. It matches how law firm sites usually grow (more practice area pages, a blog, intake integrations). Our Squarespace vs WordPress vs Wix comparison covers the platform decision in more depth. The rest of this guide assumes WordPress.

Step 1: Which Hostinger plan should a law firm choose?

Hostinger’s WordPress hosting page lists three main tiers. The figures below are the promotional terms shown there in November 2026, paid upfront for 48 months, excluding tax. Hostinger changes promotions frequently, so confirm everything on Hostinger’s pricing page.

All three plans show a free domain for the first year and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Hostinger also notes that its “unlimited” features are subject to a Fair Usage Policy. Note that Hostinger’s pages are not fully consistent on Premium’s backup wording, so read the comparison table at checkout.

Which plan for which firm?

  • Premium: a solo lawyer with one simple site and a very tight budget, who is comfortable that backups run weekly.
  • Unlimited: most small firms. Daily backups matter if you add intake forms or publish often, and unlimited mailboxes cover staff addresses in year one.
  • Cloud Startup: only if the site has grown heavy (many pages, large media) or you want on-demand backups.

Two cost points to plan for: the low monthly price requires the long term, and the renewal rate is several times higher than the promo. Multiply the renewal monthly price by 12 when you build the firm’s budget. For wider cost context, see how much a law firm website costs. If you are weighing Hostinger against other hosts, see our Hostinger vs SiteGround comparison.

Step 2: How do you choose and register the domain?

The domain is your web address and the base of your email addresses (for example, you@yourfirm.com). Hostinger’s plans show a free domain for one year, after which it renews at the regular rate, so check the renewal price for your extension before you pick it.

  • Use the firm name or lawyer name. Avoid hyphens and numbers.
  • Compare extensions in our .law vs .com vs .attorney guide. Eligibility rules and renewal costs differ.
  • Register the domain in the firm’s name with a firm-controlled email address, not a personal one that may disappear. See the best domain registrars for law firms if you prefer to keep the domain separate from hosting. Our GoDaddy domain walkthrough shows that route.

Keeping the domain at a separate registrar from the host is a common risk-reduction choice, since losing access to one account does not lock you out of both.

Step 3: How do you install WordPress with Hostinger hPanel?

hPanel is Hostinger’s control panel. According to Hostinger’s WordPress installation tutorial, there are two routes, and the menu names may change, so treat these as a guide.

Route A: the onboarding wizard (new plan)

  1. After purchase, follow the onboarding chat. On an existing plan, go to Websites, then Create site, then WordPress.
  2. Enter your domain and keep the suggested server region unless most visitors are elsewhere.
  3. Create the WordPress admin login: language, admin email and a strong administrator password.
  4. Choose “Build from scratch” for a blank site, or the AI option for a generated starter. For a law firm, we suggest blank; AI-generated placeholder text is easy to leave behind by mistake.

Route B: the WordPress installer (existing hosting site)

  1. In hPanel, open Websites, choose Manage site, then Website, then WordPress Install, and click Install.
  2. Enter the website title, administrator email, username and password. Do not use “admin” as the username.
  3. Under Advanced you can set an installation path. Leave “Create new database” selected.
  4. Hostinger’s tutorial suggests updating only to minor versions automatically so security and bug-fix updates apply. Then click Install.

Hostinger warns that the installer overwrites existing files in the target site, so back up first if there is content you want to keep.

Step 4: Is SSL included, and what about backups?

SSL (the padlock and https:// in the address bar) encrypts traffic between a visitor and your site. Hostinger’s tutorial says SSL activates automatically once your domain connects to the server, and that SSL and Force HTTPS are on by default. If you see a “connection is not private” warning right after launch, it is usually still being set up. Confirm the status on the hPanel dashboard and test every page, since mixed http/https content is a common leftover.

Backups are copies of your site you can restore after a mistake or hack. Per Hostinger’s plan page, Premium backs up weekly and Unlimited and Cloud Startup daily. Set this up before you add content, and then:

  • Look at the Backups section in hPanel and note the schedule.
  • Do one test restore on a staging copy, or at least confirm you know where the restore button is.
  • Keep an independent off-site copy too. WordPress’s own hardening guide advises regular backups of files and the database, with several past snapshots, and testing that you can restore them.

Step 5: What pages does a law firm website need?

A theme (the design layer) gives you the layout; the pages carry the value. Start with our list of WordPress themes for law firms. A fast, well-supported theme beats a flashy one. Then build these pages in this order:

  • Home: who you help, where, and one clear way to contact you.
  • Practice area pages: one page per service, not one page listing everything. See how to write practice area pages.
  • Attorney bio pages: credentials, bar admissions, approach. See how to write an attorney bio.
  • Contact / intake: phone, address, hours and a form. Keep the form minimal and avoid collecting confidential case details. See how to add a secure contact form.
  • Privacy policy and disclaimer: including a notice that sending a message does not create an attorney-client relationship, worded to your state bar’s advertising rules. Ask your state bar or counsel what is required.

Also review accessibility from the start; our accessibility guide explains WCAG basics.

Step 6: How do you set up business email on Hostinger?

Hostinger plans show mailboxes for the first year (Premium: 2 per site; Unlimited and Cloud Startup: unlimited per site). Hostinger also sells standalone Business Email plans; its email hosting page lists Starter, Standard and Premium tiers with 5 GB, 20 GB and 50 GB per mailbox, and says the page does not state where data is stored. If client confidentiality or storage location matters to the firm, ask Hostinger directly.

Many firms prefer a dedicated email suite with stronger admin and compliance controls. Compare options in Google Workspace vs Microsoft 365 for law firms, and set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC using our business email guide. For sensitive client communications, see law firm email encryption.

Step 7: What security basics should you do on a new WordPress site?

Law firm sites hold contact details and are trusted by clients, so a hacked site is costly. The WordPress.org hardening guide lists the fundamentals:

  • Keep WordPress, themes and plugins updated; enable automatic updates where appropriate.
  • Use long, unique passwords from a password manager and turn on two-step authentication. Our password manager guide compares options.
  • Avoid common admin usernames like “admin”.
  • Install only plugins you need and remove unused ones.
  • Back up and test restores.

Then add a security plugin and work through our law firm website security checklist. See WordPress security plugins for law firms, and our Sucuri review if you want a cloud firewall. If something goes wrong, read what to do if your law firm website is hacked.

Step 8: What should you check before launch?

Work through the checklist above, then test on a phone and a laptop, submit the form yourself, and confirm a human reads the inbox. Next, set up measurement with GA4 and Search Console, and claim your Google Business Profile. Our free website checklist and local SEO checklist cover what comes next. Speed matters too; see law firm website speed.

When should a law firm choose managed hosting instead of Hostinger?

Shared and cloud plans like Hostinger’s give you a server and tools, but you remain responsible for the WordPress layer: updates, plugin choices, security and restores. Consider managed WordPress hosting if:

  • No one at the firm, or on retainer, will update and monitor the site.
  • You want the host to handle malware cleanup, staging and expert support.
  • The site generates enough business that downtime or a hack would cost more than the price gap.

See our Kinsta review, WP Engine review and the three-way comparison. Budget cost is only part of the picture; website maintenance takes time or money wherever you host. Browse more in our tool comparisons or start from Start Here.

FAQ

How long does it take to build a law firm website on Hostinger?

Installing WordPress takes minutes. Hostinger’s tutorial says installation takes about two minutes. The real time goes into writing pages, collecting bios and photos, and testing, which commonly takes days to weeks.

Is Hostinger good for a law firm website?

It can be a good-value option for a simple brochure site if someone handles updates and backups. Our Hostinger review covers strengths and limits in detail.

Does Hostinger include a free domain and SSL?

Hostinger’s plan pages show a free domain for the first year, and its tutorial says SSL and Force HTTPS are on by default once the domain connects. Renewal prices for the domain are separate; see Hostinger’s pricing page.

Does Hostinger back up my WordPress site daily?

Per its plan page, Unlimited and Cloud Startup have daily backups, and Premium has weekly. Always confirm the current schedule in hPanel and keep an independent copy.

Can I use Hostinger Website Builder instead of WordPress?

Yes, and it is faster to start. The trade-off is less flexibility and a harder move later. Most firms planning to grow content and SEO choose WordPress.

How much will Hostinger cost after the first term?

As of November 2026, the page showed renewals of $10.99/mo (Premium), $16.99/mo (Unlimited) and $25.99/mo (Cloud Startup). Prices change, so check before you buy.

Conclusion: next steps

  • Decide WordPress vs builder (we suggest WordPress) and pick a plan, with Unlimited as the default.
  • Register the domain, install WordPress and confirm SSL and backups on day one.
  • Write the four core pages and a minimal intake form before launch.
  • Lock down logins and updates, then run the launch checklist.
  • If maintenance is not realistic in-house, price managed hosting or a maintenance service.

title.raw: Best WordPress Security Plugins for Law Firms: Wordfence vs Sucuri vs Solid Security (2026)
title.rendered: Best WordPress Security Plugins for Law Firms: Wordfence vs Sucuri vs Solid Security (2026)

content.raw:
Quick answer: For most small law firms, the best WordPress security plugin setup is one firewall plus one login-hardening layer. Use Wordfence if you want an endpoint firewall and malware scanner inside WordPress. Use Sucuri if you want a cloud firewall and cleanup service in front of your site. Use Solid Security (now sold as Kadence Security) if your main gap is login protection. Do not run two firewall plugins at once.

Key takeaways

  • A WordPress security plugin reduces risk. It does not replace updates, backups, strong passwords and a good host.
  • Wordfence is an endpoint firewall (runs inside WordPress). Sucuri is a cloud firewall (sits in front of your site). Solid Security focuses on hardening and login security.
  • Wordfence Free delays new firewall rules and malware signatures by 30 days. Paid plans get them in real time.
  • Pick one firewall. Stacking two can cause conflicts and slowdowns.
  • Check what your host already provides before you pay for more.

Why does a law firm need a WordPress security plugin?

A law firm site holds contact-form inquiries, staff logins and sometimes client portals. A compromise can expose that information or send visitors to spam pages. ABA Model Rule 1.6(c) says a lawyer must make reasonable efforts to prevent inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure of, or access to, information relating to a client's representation. A security plugin is one reasonable, documentable step. Your state bar may add its own expectations, so check with it.

This guide compares the plugins. For the full list of what to lock down (updates, backups, SSL, user roles), use our law firm website security checklist. We will not repeat it here.

How we compared these plugins

This comparison is based on each vendor's official pricing page, plugin listing and documentation as of November 2026. We have not run hands-on tests, and we give no scores or ratings. Prices change, so confirm on the vendor's page before buying.

What is the difference between an endpoint firewall and a cloud firewall?

A firewall is software that blocks bad requests before they do damage. An endpoint firewall runs inside your WordPress install. A cloud (DNS-level) firewall filters traffic before it reaches your server, which requires pointing your domain's DNS at the provider.

  • Endpoint (Wordfence): Wordfence describes its firewall as protecting the site at the endpoint, with deep WordPress integration. It runs on your server, so it uses your server's resources.
  • Cloud (Sucuri): traffic is filtered on Sucuri's servers first. Sucuri lists a CDN effect that reduces server load, and an HTTPS connection through its firewall. Setup involves a DNS change. Our Cloudflare for law firm websites guide explains how that kind of DNS-level setup works.
  • Hardening (Solid Security): not primarily a firewall. It tightens login, passwords, lockouts and file monitoring.

Wordfence vs Sucuri vs Solid Security: comparison table

How much do Wordfence, Sucuri and Solid Security cost?

Prices as of November 2026, from the vendors' own pages. All are annual unless noted.

Wordfence pricing

Per the Wordfence pricing page: Free is $0; Premium is $149 per year; Care is $590 per year; Response is $1,250 per year. Free has a 30-day delay on firewall rules and malware signatures. Premium adds real-time rules and signatures, a premium IP blocklist, country blocking, an audit log and ticket support. Care adds hands-on help from an analyst (install, configure, optimize, monitoring, malware removal). Response adds 24/7/365 incident response with a 1-hour response time. Wordfence says the licence is per site; see its FAQ on how many licences you need.

Sucuri pricing

Per Sucuri's plans page: the Website Security Platform is billed yearly at $229 (Basic), $339 (Pro) and $549 (Business) for one site, with unlimited cleanups and different scan frequencies and response times. A firewall-only product (CloudProxy) is billed monthly at $9.99 (Basic) or $19.98 (Pro). Some per-tier details were unclear on the page, so confirm exact features with Sucuri before buying.

Solid Security pricing

Solid Security, formerly iThemes Security, is now branded Kadence Security on its WordPress.org listing ("by Nexcess"), and the old solidwp.com address redirects to Liquid Web's Kadence pages. The free plugin is on WordPress.org. Pro features are now sold inside Kadence bundles on Liquid Web's Kadence page, which listed a one-site plan at $350 per year when we checked. Those bundles also include other products, so see the vendor's pricing page for what applies to you.

What does each plugin do well?

Wordfence: the all-in-one scanner and firewall

According to its plugin listing, Wordfence includes a web application firewall, malware scanner, login security (2FA, passkeys, CAPTCHA, blocking known-compromised admin passwords), brute-force limits and vulnerability checks. The scanner compares core, theme and plugin files with the WordPress.org repository. Best for: a firm that wants one plugin handling most security tasks.

Sucuri: the cloud firewall plus cleanup

Sucuri's plans bundle a cloud firewall with monitoring and unlimited cleanups. Best for: a firm that wants a vendor to fix a hacked site and does not mind a DNS change. Because filtering happens off your server, it can reduce load on small hosting plans.

Solid Security: login and hardening

The listing shows free features such as 2FA, password requirements, banning users, local brute-force protection, file change detection and a site scanner. Pro adds items like passwordless login, trusted devices, user logging and Patchstack virtual patching. Best for: a firm that has a firewall at the host and wants to tighten logins.

Do WordPress security plugins slow down your site?

They can. An endpoint firewall and scanner run on your own server, so scans and request filtering use its resources. Wordfence lets you schedule scans. A cloud firewall moves filtering off your server but adds a network hop and DNS setup. Measure your pages before and after; our law firm website speed guide explains how.

Can you use two security plugins together?

Run only one firewall. Two plugins that both filter requests and rewrite server rules can block each other or double the load. It is fine to pair a firewall with a login-hardening tool, but disable overlapping features (for example, turn off duplicate brute-force or 2FA settings) so you only have one of each. The same goes for a cloud firewall plus an endpoint firewall: choose a primary and test carefully. Our best WordPress plugins for law firms list covers the rest of a sensible plugin stack.

Does your host already cover security?

Often partly. Kinsta's plan page lists enterprise DDoS protection, and its menu lists bot protection and vulnerability protection. SiteGround describes AI-powered bot protection and 24/7 monitoring. Those features are on the host side, so you may not need a paid firewall plugin. They do not replace WordPress-level steps like 2FA, strong passwords and removing unused plugins. Compare hosts in our best law firm hosting guide.

Which WordPress security plugin should a law firm choose?

  • Solo with managed hosting: free login hardening (Solid Security or Wordfence login features), 2FA on every admin, updates on, and use the host's protections.
  • Small firm on shared hosting, DIY: Wordfence Free at minimum; consider Premium ($149/yr) for real-time rules.
  • Firm that wants cleanup included: compare Sucuri's platform plans and Wordfence Care.
  • Firm with a developer or maintenance plan: have them choose and monitor it; see law firm website maintenance.

How do you set up a security plugin safely?

  1. Take a full backup first.
  2. Install one firewall plugin only.
  3. Turn on 2FA for every administrator and editor.
  4. Enable login attempt limits and email alerts to a monitored address.
  5. Run a first scan and review results before deleting anything.
  6. Use a password manager so staff can use unique passwords.
  7. Test the contact form and key pages afterward.
  8. Recheck monthly and after major updates.

FAQ

What is the best WordPress security plugin for a law firm?

There is no single best. Wordfence is the most complete single plugin, Sucuri suits firms wanting a cloud firewall with cleanup, and Solid Security suits login hardening. Choose by the gap you need to fill.

Is Wordfence Free enough?

It covers a firewall, scanner and login protection, but firewall rules and malware signatures arrive 30 days late compared with Premium, per Wordfence's pricing page. Whether that is acceptable depends on your risk tolerance.

Is Solid Security the same as iThemes Security?

Yes, it is the renamed product. Its WordPress.org listing now shows the name Kadence Security and says "formerly iThemes Security". Some documentation may still use the older names.

Do security plugins make me compliant with Rule 1.6?

No. Rule 1.6(c) calls for reasonable efforts, and a plugin is one piece. Policies, access control, vendor choices and training also matter. Ask your state bar or ethics counsel for specifics.

Will a plugin remove malware for me?

Wordfence offers cleanup on its Care and Response plans, and Sucuri lists unlimited cleanups on its plans. Read each vendor's terms for scope and timing.

Do I need Sucuri if my host has a firewall?

Often not. Check what your host provides and what it does not, then fill only the gaps.

Conclusion and next steps

  • Check your host's security features.
  • Pick one firewall and one login-hardening layer.
  • Turn on 2FA and login limits today.
  • Work through the security checklist.
  • Browse our tool comparisons or start here for other decisions.

Want this handled for you? ProSiteGuide builds and maintains fast, secure WordPress sites for law firms. Book a free consultation.

For a deeper look at the cloud firewall option, read our Sucuri review for law firms.

Do security plugins make me compliant with Rule 1.6?

No. Rule 1.6(c) calls for reasonable efforts, and a plugin is one piece. Policies, access control, vendor choices and training also matter. Ask your state bar or ethics counsel for specifics.

Wordfence offers cleanup on its Care and Response plans, and Sucuri lists unlimited cleanups on its plans. Read each vendor’s terms for scope and timing.

Often not. Check what your host provides and what it does not, then fill only the gaps.

  • Pick one firewall and one login-hardening layer.

title.raw: Best Password Managers for Law Firms: 1Password vs Bitwarden vs Keeper (2026)
title.rendered: Best Password Managers for Law Firms: 1Password vs Bitwarden vs Keeper (2026)

content.raw:
Quick answer: the best password manager for law firms is the one your staff will actually use for every shared login, with admin controls to remove access fast. On published prices as of November 2026, Bitwarden Teams is $4.00 per user per month billed annually, 1Password Teams Starter Pack is $2.49 per user per month for 10 to 20 users, and 1Password Business is $8.99 per user per month. Keeper lists its Business plans as annual but its page did not show a number when we checked, so use Keeper's pricing page.

Key takeaways

  • A password manager for law firms is a practical way to show "reasonable efforts" under ABA Model Rule 1.6(c). It does not replace other safeguards.
  • Published business prices differ widely: $2.49 (1Password Starter Pack, 10 to 20 users), $4.00 (Bitwarden Teams) up to $8.99 (1Password Business). Keeper: see its pricing page.
  • Bitwarden Teams has no SSO; SSO is in Bitwarden Enterprise at $6.00. Keeper lists SSO (SAML 2.0) under Enterprise.
  • Offboarding matters more than features: the day someone leaves, you need to cut access and rotate shared logins.
  • This comparison is based on vendor pricing pages, documentation and terms. We have not hands-on tested these products.

How we compared these password managers

We read each vendor's official business pricing page, its security or audit page, and the help pages that describe features. We did not run hands-on tests, and we give no scores or star ratings. Prices are in US dollars, exclude tax, and are as of November 2026. Vendors change prices, so confirm at checkout.

Why does a law firm need a password manager?

A password manager is software that stores logins in an encrypted vault, fills them in for you and generates strong unique passwords. For a law firm the main risks are reused passwords and shared credentials kept in spreadsheets, sticky notes or email. A single compromised login to your email, case software or bank portal can expose client information.

ABA Model Rule 1.6(c) says a lawyer must make reasonable efforts to prevent inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure of, or unauthorized access to, information relating to the representation. ABA Formal Opinion 477R (2017) discusses securing client communications and says reasonable efforts depend on factors such as the sensitivity of the information, the likelihood of disclosure without safeguards, the cost of safeguards and how much they burden the lawyer's work. A password manager is a low-cost safeguard that fits that analysis. This is general information, not legal advice. Check your state bar's rules and ethics opinions, which may add requirements.

How much do 1Password, Bitwarden and Keeper cost for a law firm?

The table uses each vendor's official business pricing page (1Password, Bitwarden, Keeper), as of November 2026.

For a five-lawyer firm with five staff (10 users), 1Password's Starter Pack is a flat $24.95 per month on its page. At published list prices, Bitwarden Teams would be 10 x $4.00 = $40 per month, and 1Password Business 10 x $8.99 = $89.90 per month. These are simple multiplications of list prices, not quotes.

Which password manager is best for a small law firm?

1Password: best if you want the cheapest published entry plan

1Password's Starter Pack covers 10 to 20 people at a low flat rate. The Business plan adds role-based vault sharing and permissions, broader admin and reporting, Watchtower security alerts and integrations with identity providers such as Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin and Duo, per its business pricing page. The page did not clearly show SSO by plan, so confirm SSO availability with 1Password before buying. Its personal plans also list passkey support, two-factor authentication and a Secret Key used with your account password. A 14-day free trial is listed with no credit card required.

Bitwarden: best for transparent pricing and published audits

Bitwarden Teams includes collections (its term for shared groups of logins), user groups, event and audit logs, directory sync, SCIM provisioning, organization two-factor login via Duo, vault health reports for weak, reused or exposed passwords, and passkey management, per its business pricing page. SSO, policies, custom roles, account recovery and self-hosting are Enterprise-only. Both plans offer a free trial; the page does not state the length.

Keeper: best for firms that want a quote-based plan and listed compliance programs

Keeper's pricing page lists an encrypted vault, admin console and credential sharing on Business Starter; shared team folders, delegated admin and a free Family Plan for each user on Business; and SCIM, AD/LDAP, SSO, advanced 2FA and role-based access control on Enterprise. Passkey sharing is listed, but the page does not say which tier includes it. BreachWatch dark web monitoring appeared only as an add-on reference, so ask Keeper whether it is included in the plan you want.

How do shared vaults work for lawyers and staff?

A shared vault (1Password), collection (Bitwarden) or shared folder (Keeper) is a group of logins that only chosen people can open. Typical law firm examples are the court e-filing account, case management software, the bank portal and the firm's social accounts. Set access by role: paralegals may need the e-filing login but not the bank portal. Give each person their own individual vault for personal logins so firm and personal items stay separate. If your logins live in Microsoft 365 or Google, see our guides to Microsoft 365 setup for law firms and Google Workspace setup for law firms.

What about SSO, 2FA and passkeys?

Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds a second proof, such as a code, after the password. Single sign-on (SSO) lets staff sign in to the password manager with the identity they already use at work, so the firm controls one login. Passkeys are phishing-resistant sign-ins that replace a password with a cryptographic key on your device. Among these vendors, Bitwarden clearly puts SSO in Enterprise only, Keeper lists SAML 2.0 SSO in Enterprise, and 1Password lists identity-provider integrations on Business. For a firm of ten or fewer, 2FA on the vault plus unique passwords usually covers the biggest risks; SSO is more useful as headcount grows. Passkey storage is listed by Bitwarden (all accounts), 1Password (personal plans) and Keeper (tier not specified).

How do admin controls and offboarding work?

Offboarding is the most important admin feature for a law firm. When a paralegal or associate leaves, you must remove their access and change any shared password they could see. The vault cannot do the second part automatically.

  1. Suspend or remove the user in the admin console or directory.
  2. List what they could reach from their vault and group memberships.
  3. Rotate shared logins such as bank, e-filing and case software passwords.
  4. Record it in a simple log: date, items rotated, who did it.

Bitwarden Teams lists event and audit logs and directory sync. Keeper lists delegated admin on Business and reporting add-ons. 1Password lists broader admin and reporting on Business. Check each vendor's documentation for exactly what the admin can see, and decide who the firm's admins are before you buy.

Do these tools include breach and dark-web monitoring?

Breach monitoring checks whether your stored logins appear in known data leaks. 1Password lists Watchtower alerts for weak or compromised credentials on its personal plans and on Business. Bitwarden Teams lists vault health reports for weak, reused or exposed passwords. Keeper lists Dark Web Monitoring as an add-on reference on its business page; confirm what is included. Monitoring tells you a password is exposed; you still have to change it.

What security audits do the vendors publish?

Audits are a vendor-reported signal, not a guarantee. Here is what each publishes on its own pages.

Which should my firm choose?

  • 10 to 20 people and a tight budget: price 1Password Teams Starter Pack against Bitwarden Teams.
  • Want SSO with a published price: Bitwarden Enterprise ($6.00) or 1Password Business ($8.99, confirm SSO).
  • Solo lawyer: 1Password Business has a 1-user minimum; Bitwarden has no stated minimum on its page.
  • Want vendor guidance on plan and add-ons: ask Keeper for a quote.

Before buying, use the free trial with two people and one shared vault, and import an export of your current logins. Pair the manager with the basics in our law firm website security checklist, encrypted email as covered in law firm email encryption and a proper law firm business email setup. For more software choices, see our tool comparisons and Start Here guide.

FAQ

Is it ethical for lawyers to use a cloud password manager?

Generally the question is whether you made reasonable efforts under Rule 1.6(c). Vendors describe encrypted vaults, but you should read the terms, use 2FA and check your state bar's guidance. This is not legal advice.

Is Bitwarden or 1Password cheaper for a law firm?

On published list prices, 1Password's Starter Pack ($2.49 per user per month, 10 to 20 users) is lowest, then Bitwarden Teams ($4.00), then 1Password Business ($8.99). Bitwarden has no user minimum stated on its page.

Does Bitwarden Teams include SSO?

No. Its pricing page lists passwordless SSO as Enterprise-only ($6.00 per user per month billed annually).

Can staff share logins safely?

Yes, through shared vaults, collections or folders with role-based access. Avoid sending passwords by email or chat.

What should we do when an employee leaves?

Remove the account, review what they could access and rotate shared passwords, then log it.

Conclusion and next steps

Pick two vendors, confirm the current price and SSO terms on their pages, run a trial with one shared vault, and write a one-page policy: who is the admin, which logins are shared and how offboarding works. Then roll it out to everyone at once.
